units.title: Official and working Russian: the заявление, the complaint, the email, the telephone and the register ladder

lessons.title: The заявление: the fixed layout of a Russian application, and why every slot is a case ending
lessons.explanation:
Official Russian begins with layout, not with a sentence. A заявление (za-yav-LYE-nee-ye), 'application, written request', is the document a private person addresses to an institution, and it is built from slots that a clerk can find without reading: the addressee in the upper right corner, the applicant beneath it, the single word заявление in the middle, and a body that opens with прошу (pra-SHOO), 'I ask'. The samples printed in a Russian university's own regulation show the pattern with unusual clarity. The ДВГМУ Положение о порядке предоставления академических отпусков (pa-la-ZHYE-nee-ye a pa-RYAT-kye pre-das-tav-LYE-nee-ya a-ka-dee-MEE-ches-kikh OT-poo-skaf), 'regulation on the procedure for granting academic leave', prints a sample that runs: Ректору ДВГМУ (RYEK-ta-roo dee-veh-geh-em-OO), 'to the rector of the Far Eastern State Medical University'; К. В. Жмеренецкому (zhmye-ree-NYETS-ka-moo); студента второго курса лечебного факультета группы 201 (stoo-DYEN-ta fta-RO-va KOR-sa lee-CHEB-na-va fa-kool-TYE-ta GROO-py dvey-SYOT pir-va-va), 'of a second-year student of the medical faculty, group 201'; заявление; then Прошу предоставить мне академический отпуск в связи с призывом в Вооруженные Силы Российской Федерации (pra-SHOO pree-das-TA-veet mnye a-ka-dee-MEE-ches-keey OT-poosk v SVYA-zee s pree-ZY-vam v va-ee-ROO-zhon-ny-ye SEE-ly Ra-SEE-skaoy Fee-de-RA-ts-ee), 'I ask that I be granted academic leave in connection with conscription into the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation'; then Приложение (pree-la-ZHYE-nee-ye), 'enclosure', with a numbered list; then Дата and Подпись (DA-ta, POD-pees), 'date' and 'signature'. Nothing in that block is decoration. Ректору is dative because the paper is addressed to him, студента is genitive because the applicant is named as the source of the request, отпуск is accusative because просить takes a direct object, and с призывом is instrumental because в связи с governs the instrumental that lesson 63 established. Change one ending and the document stops being a заявление: a nominative addressee turns it into a letter, a first-person applicant turns it into an explanation, and a missing ground turns it into an unanswerable note that the office will send back.

The applicant block has two attested variants, and both are correct. University templates often write the bare genitive, студента второго курса, while offices that deal with the public usually write от plus the genitive, от Петровой Марии Сергеевны (at pee-TO-ro-vay ma-REE-ee syer-GYE-yev-ny), 'from Maria Sergeevna Petrova'. What is never accepted is the nominative, because the header is not a sentence and has no subject. The name order is surname, first name, patronymic, and all three decline: Петровой, Марии, Сергеевны, not Петрова, Мария, Сергеевна. The addressee's должность (DOLZH-nast), 'position', takes the dative as well, so директору Соколову (dee-RYEK-ta-roo sa-ka-LO-voo), 'to director Sokolov', has a dative noun and a dative surname that agree in case but not in gender, and the company name in quotation marks stays as it is, ООО «Север» (a-O-O SYE-veer), 'Sever Limited Liability Company'.
lessons.example:
Here is a complete заявление of the commonest workplace kind, asking for leave without pay. Upper right: Генеральному директору ООО «Север» Соколову Андрею Петровичу (gye-nee-RAL-na-moo dee-RYEK-ta-roo a-O-O SYE-veer sa-ka-LO-voo an-DRYE-yu peet-RO-vee-choo), 'to Andrei Petrovich Sokolov, general director of Sever LLC'. Beneath it: от менеджера отдела продаж Петровой Марии Сергеевны (at MYE-nee-je-ra at-DYE-la pra-DAZH pee-TO-ro-vay ma-REE-ee syer-GYE-yev-ny), 'from Maria Sergeevna Petrova, manager of the sales department'. Then the title word on its own line, then the request: Прошу предоставить мне отпуск без сохранения заработной платы на три календарных дня, с 12 по 14 мая 2026 года, в связи с семейными обстоятельствами (pra-SHOO pree-das-TA-veet mnye OT-poosk byez sa-khra-NYE-nee-ya ZA-ra-bat-nay PLA-ty na tree ka-leen-DAR-nykh dnya, s dvee-NA-tsa-ta-va pa chye-TYR-na-tsa-ta-ye MA-ya dvee TY-see-chee dvey-SYOT dva-tsat shes-TO-va GO-da, v SVYA-zee s sye-MYEY-ny-mee ab-sta-YA-tyel-stva-mee), 'I ask that I be granted leave without pay for three calendar days, from 12 to 14 May 2026, in connection with family circumstances'. Then Основание: статья 128 Трудового кодекса Российской Федерации (as-na-VA-nee-ye, stat-YA STO DVA-tsat va-see-MO-va troo-da-VO-va KO-dek-sa), 'ground: article 128 of the Labour Code of the Russian Federation'. Then Приложение: копия свидетельства о браке (pree-la-ZHYE-nee-ye, KO-pee-ya svee-DYE-tyel-stva a BRA-kye), 'enclosure: copy of the marriage certificate'. Then the date and the signature, written as М. С. Петрова, initials first.

Four details repay attention. Отпуск is accusative, but на три календарных дня is a duration phrase that takes the accusative after на while the numeral keeps the noun in the genitive plural, which is the counting rule of lesson 54. The dates use с plus the genitive and по plus the accusative, and года stands in the genitive after the day and month, a convention that documents keep and conversation often drops. В связи с governs the instrumental, so обстоятельствами and never обстоятельства. And Основание is a slot, not a sentence: a colon, a noun phrase, no verb. If the office's template has no Основание line, the same ground moves into the body as a dependent phrase: на основании статьи 128 Трудового кодекса (na as-na-VA-nee-ee stat-EE STO DVA-tsat va-see-MO-va troo-da-VO-va KO-dek-sa), 'on the basis of article 128 of the Labour Code'.

Now the same request written the way learners usually write it: Я, Петрова Мария Сергеевна, менеджер отдела продаж, хочу взять отпуск на три дня по семейным обстоятельствам (ya, pee-TO-ro-va ma-REE-ya syer-GYE-yev-na, MYE-nee-jer at-DYE-la pra-DAZH, kha-CHOO vzyat OT-poosk na tree dnya pa sye-MYEY-nym ab-sta-YA-tyel-stvam), 'I, Maria Sergeevna Petrova, sales manager, want to take three days off for family reasons'. Every word is grammatical and the document is unusable. The pronoun я turns a form into a personal statement, хочу взять replaces the performative прошу предоставить with a description of a wish, по семейным обстоятельствам uses the wrong preposition for the template, and the applicant's name now appears in the body while the header stays empty. Rewrite it into the slots and the facts do not change at all: same dates, same reason, same endings from lesson 53, and a paper the office can file.
lessons.question: You draft «Я, Иванов Иван, студент второго курса, прошу дать мне академический отпуск». A clerk returns it. What is wrong, and what does the corrected document look like?
lessons.answer: The first person belongs in the body only: a заявление puts the applicant in the header as a genitive phrase (студента второго курса Иванова Ивана or от студента Иванова Ивана), opens the body with прошу, and uses the collocation предоставить отпуск rather than дать.
lessons.distractor: Only the word дать is wrong; the pronoun я and the name in the body are normal in Russian documents and the clerk simply prefers a different font.
lessons.correction: Two things are wrong and they have different causes. The layout error is the pronoun and the name in the body: the header already identifies the applicant, and the body of a заявление contains only the request and its ground, so я, Иванов Иван duplicates a slot and pushes the document towards the genre of объяснительная (ab-yas-NEE-tyel-na-ya), 'written explanation', where the writer does speak about himself in the first person. The lexical error is дать отпуск, which is what a person says to a colleague but not what a document asks for: the collocation is предоставить отпуск (pree-das-TA-veet OT-poosk), and предоставить is the verb of official granting throughout, as in предоставить документы, предоставить отсрочку. The corrected version reads: Декану факультета Петрову И. И. от студента второго курса Иванова И. И. заявление. Прошу предоставить мне академический отпуск с 1 сентября 2026 года в связи с медицинскими показаниями. Приложение: заключение врачебной комиссии. Note also that the name order reverses between header and body prose: the header is surname first because the office files by surname, while in the body a full name would be first name and patronymic.

depth.definitions: Реквизит (ree-kvee-ZEET), 'requisite', is any element a document type requires, and a заявление needs about eight of them. Адресат (ad-ree-SAT) is the addressee, the official or body the paper goes to, and stands in the dative; адресант (ad-ree-SANT) is the sender, standing in the genitive, either after от or as a bare genitive phrase. Шапка (SHAP-ka), literally 'cap', is the colloquial name for the header block in the upper right corner, while official usage says реквизиты. The просительная часть (pra-SEE-tyel-na-ya CHAST), 'request section', is the sentence introduced by прошу, and it is the only place where the document speaks in the first person. Основание (as-na-VA-nee-ye) is the legal or factual ground, usually a colon phrase citing a statute; приложение (pree-la-ZHYE-nee-ye) is an enclosure, numbered when there are several; виза (VEE-za) is an intermediate official's approving signature, which the university regulation requires from the dean before the rector sees the paper. Prerequisites: the dative recipient of lesson 61, the genitive of lesson 53, the accusative of lesson 51, the instrumental after с in lesson 63, the administrative register of lesson 92, and the written politeness routine of lesson 97.
depth.mechanism: The grammar of the header is the grammar of a sentence that is never written. A заявление is адресовано (ad-ree-SO-va-na), 'addressed', to somebody, and адресовать takes the dative, so the addressee occupies the dative whatever the body says. The applicant is the source, and Russian marks a source with the genitive, the case of origin and possession, which is why the applicant block is от Петровой or simply студента Петрова with no verb at all. The body is a performative: прошу does not report a wish, it performs the request, which is why the first person singular is right there and wrong in the header, and why прошу is followed by an infinitive (предоставить, перевести, разрешить, считать) rather than a finite verb. Because the slots are fixed, the only free variables are the endings, and that is what makes the document a grammar exercise: correct endings and the layout follows; incorrect endings and no amount of polite wording repairs it. The order of the slots is also a reading technology. A clerk scanning the corner learns who is asking and of whom, then reads one sentence, then checks the enclosures against the list, and never has to reconstruct the request from prose.
depth.secondExample: A transfer application shows the same machinery with a second infinitive and a different ground. Генеральному директору ООО «Север» Соколову А. П. от менеджера отдела продаж Петровой М. С. заявление. Прошу перевести меня на должность старшего менеджера с 1 июня 2026 года в связи с расширением отдела (pra-SHOO pee-ree-vees-TEE mee-NYA na DOLZH-nast STAR-she-va MYE-nee-je-ra s PIR-va-va EY-oo-nya dvee TY-see-chee dva-tsat shes-TO-va GO-da v SVYA-zee s rass-shee-RYE-nee-em at-DYE-la), 'I ask to be transferred to the position of senior manager from 1 June 2026 in connection with the expansion of the department'. Three observations. Перевести меня keeps the accusative of the person moved and adds на должность plus the accusative of the post, so the sentence carries two accusatives with different jobs, one for the object and one for the destination, exactly as the motion phrases of lesson 67 do with places. The date phrase с 1 июня is genitive because с marks the starting point, and 1 июня stays ordinal-genitive even though it is written as a digit. В связи с расширением отдела is the instrumental again, and this time the noun is a nominalisation, расширение, which unit 1 returns to in lesson 125: official style prefers в связи с расширением to потому что отдел расширяется. Note finally that the ground here is factual rather than legal, so no article is cited and the sentence ends with the reason instead of a colon and a statute.
depth.mistake: Three errors recur, and each has a diagnostic. The first is a nominative addressee: «Ректор университета Иванов» at the top, copied from an English letter's inside address. Diagnostic: find the first noun in the corner and ask what case it is in; if it is nominative, the paper is not addressed to anybody. The second is a first-person body that narrates rather than requests: «Я хочу взять отпуск, потому что у меня семейные обстоятельства». Diagnostic: cover the first three words; if the sentence still describes the writer's feelings, it belongs in an объяснительная, not a заявление. The third is a broken collocation: дать отпуск, сделать заявление in the sense of 'submit an application' (сделать заявление means 'to make a public statement'), or представить отпуск. Diagnostic: check the verb against the noun in a dictionary entry for the noun, not for the verb, because the noun is what selects its verb. A fourth, smaller error is the date: 12.05.2026 is acceptable in a form field but in a running document the convention is 12 мая 2026 г., with the year abbreviated as г. and the month in the genitive. Learners who write 12 мая 2026 год produce a nominative year that no Russian office writes.
depth.application: Write two заявления of your own, one personal and one professional. The first asks your employer for two days of unpaid leave next month, citing article 128; the second asks a dean to allow you to retake an examination. Use the seven slots, do not write a single sentence outside прошу, and give each document a ground and an enclosure list. Then run the slot audit: hand the header alone to another learner and ask who is writing to whom, in what capacity; if they cannot answer from the header, the cases are wrong. Next, rewrite the body of the first document three ways, once with прошу предоставить, once with прошу разрешить, and once with the bookish Прошу Вашего разрешения (pra-SHOO VA-she-va raz-ree-SHYE-nee-ya), 'I ask your permission', and decide which one the office would actually accept. Finally, compare your two documents with the samples in the university regulation cited below and list every slot where your version and the sample differ. Twenty-five minutes, and the list of differences is the real output.
depth.summary: A заявление is a layout before it is a sentence. The addressee stands in the dative in the corner, the applicant in the genitive beneath, the title word stands alone, and the body is one performative sentence with прошу plus an infinitive. The ground is either an Основание line with a colon and a statute or a dependent phrase with на основании plus the genitive or в связи с plus the instrumental. Enclosures are numbered, the date follows the Russian convention, and the signature is initials plus surname. The cases are not decoration: they are what tells the clerk who is asking, of whom, and for what.

readings.title: Дальневосточный государственный медицинский университет, Положение о порядке предоставления академических отпусков (PDF)
readings.note: Read section 2, which states that the ground for a decision is личное заявление обучающегося на имя ректора, and then the appendices, where the actual samples are printed: Приложение 2 for academic leave, Приложение 6 for returning from it, and Приложение 9 for extending it. Copy the header block and the прошу sentence verbatim into your notebook, because these are real forms that a real office accepted. Caveat: this is a local act of one university, not a federal norm, and the layout differs between institutions, so treat it as evidence of the genre rather than as the single correct template.

readings.title: Пермский национальный исследовательский политехнический университет, Положение об академических отпусках (PDF)
readings.note: Read the table of contents, then the samples on pages 12 onwards for the academic leave application and the version for postgraduate students. The value of a second university is comparison: check whether the applicant block uses от plus the genitive or the bare genitive, whether the title word is capitalised, and whether the ground sits in the body or in a separate Основание line. Caveat: like the first source this is an internal regulation, and the formatting of scanned appendices is inconsistent, so read it for the slots, not for typography.

readings.title: Википедия, «Официально-деловой стиль»
readings.note: Read the sections Описание, Особенности and Примеры. The article defines the style as the written register of legal relations and administration and lists its usual features: standardised layout, nominalisations, fixed formulas, and the absence of emotional vocabulary. That list is the background for this lesson and for lesson 125's register ladder. Caveat: the article carries a banner saying it lacks citations, and parts of it read like a summary of a textbook, so use it for the inventory of features and verify any particular claim elsewhere.

readings.title: Викисловарь, «заявление»
readings.note: Read the Значение section and the stress mark: заявле́ние, with the stress on the second syllable, which the pronunciation guide in this lesson follows. The entry distinguishes the document sense, a written request to an institution, from the general sense of a statement or declaration, and that distinction is what keeps заявление apart from объявление and объяснение. Caveat: a dictionary records meanings, not formats, so it can tell you what the word means but not how the document is laid out.

visual.title: Seven-slot заявление grid with the case written under each slot
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: the page is divided into a right-hand header column and a left-hand body column, with seven numbered slots, each carrying its case label and one model phrase. Rendered as text steps, not as an image.
steps: Step 1, draw the page. Two columns, a narrow one on the right for the header and a wide one for the body. Write slot 1 at the top right and label it адресат, dative. Put the model Генеральному директору ООО «Север» Соколову А. П. into it and underline the two dative endings.

Step 2, add the applicant. Slot 2 sits directly under slot 1, still in the right column, labelled адресант, genitive. Write от менеджера Петровой М. С. and mark the three genitive endings. Add a note: the bare genitive without от is equally acceptable in university templates.

Step 3, place the title word. Slot 3 is centred across the body column, one word, заявление, no full stop. Write beside it the observation that some offices capitalise it and some do not, and that neither choice changes the genre.

Step 4, write the request. Slot 4 is the first line of the body, labelled просительная часть. Write Прошу предоставить мне ... and then a bracket under прошу marked performative, and a bracket under the infinitive marked the only verb form allowed here.

Step 5, add the ground and the enclosures. Slot 5 is the ground, either Основание: статья 128 ТК РФ or в связи с plus the instrumental; slot 6 is Приложение with a numbered list; slot 7 is the date and signature block, initials before the surname.

Step 6, audit the grid. Read only slots 1, 2 and 4 aloud and check that a listener can say who is writing, to whom, and what is being asked. If any of the three answers needs a sentence from elsewhere on the page, a case ending is wrong and the grid has found it.

lessons.title: A complaint and a request: three letters that look alike, and the four sentences that keep them apart
lessons.explanation:
Russian distinguishes three letters that English often lumps together. Претензия (pree-TEN-zee-ya) is a claim addressed to the party that broke the agreement: it states what went wrong, cites the basis, demands a specific action within a period, and warns what happens if the period passes. Жалоба (ZHA-la-ba) is a complaint addressed to somebody who has power over the party at fault, a director, a regulator, a ministry: it asks the recipient to intervene rather than to pay. Письмо-просьба (pees-MO pras-BA), 'letter of request', asks for something without alleging any fault at all. The three share a layout, which is the layout of lesson 121: addressee in the dative at the top right, a subject line, a body, enclosures, date and signature. What separates them is the addressee and the verb of the final sentence, and getting that wrong is the mistake that costs a Russian writer most.

A претензия is built from four load-bearing sentences and any number of supporting ones. The first states the facts: «12 марта 2026 года мы заключили с вами договор на поставку оборудования» (dvee-NA-tsa-ta-va MAR-ta dvee TY-see-chee dvey-SYOT dva-tsat shes-TO-va GO-da my za-klyoo-CHEE-lee s VA-mee da-ga-VOR na pas-TAF-koo a-ba-ROO-da-va-nee-ya), 'on 12 March 2026 we concluded a supply contract with you'. The second names the breach: «Оборудование было поставлено с нарушением срока на двадцать дней» (a-ba-ROO-da-va-nee-ye BY-la pas-TAV-lee-na s na-roo-SHYE-nee-em SRO-ka na DVA-tsat dnyey), 'the equipment was delivered twenty days late'. The third cites the basis, and here the case is decided by the preposition: в соответствии с governs the instrumental, so «в соответствии со статьёй 31 Закона о защите прав потребителей» (v sa-at-VYET-stvee sa stat-YOY TREE-tsat pir-va-va za-KO-na a za-SHEE-tye praf pa-tree-BEE-tye-lyey), 'in accordance with article 31 of the Consumer Protection Act', and на основании governs the genitive, so «на основании пункта 1 статьи 29» (na as-na-VA-nee-ee POONK-ta pir-VO-va stat-EE DVA-tsat dee-VYA-ta-va), 'on the basis of point 1 of article 29'. The fourth is the demand with its period: «Прошу в течение десяти дней с момента получения настоящей претензии вернуть уплаченную сумму» (pra-SHOO v tee-CHE-nee-ye dee-see-TEE dnyey s ma-MYEN-ta pa-loo-CHE-nee-ya na-sta-YA-shchey pree-TEN-zee-ee veer-NOOT oo-pla-CHE-noo-yu SOO-moo), 'I ask that the sum paid be returned within ten days of receipt of this claim'. Then the consequence, which is what makes it a claim rather than a request: «В случае неисполнения обязательств в установленный срок мы будем вынуждены обратиться в суд» (f SLOO-cha-ye ne-ees-pal-NYE-nee-ya a-bya-ZA-tyel-stv v oo-sta-NOV-lyen-ny SROK my BOO-dem VY-noozh-dee-ny ab-ra-TEET-sya f soot), 'in the event of non-performance within the period set we will be obliged to go to court'.

The period is not invented by the writer. Article 31 of the consumer protection law says that the demands listed there подлежат удовлетворению в десятидневный срок (pat-lye-ZHAT oo-dav-lyet-va-RYE-nee-yu v dee-see-tee-DNYEV-ny SROK), 'are subject to satisfaction within a ten-day period', so the letter echoes the statute's own words and the number becomes arguable in law rather than a mood. In a commercial contract the period comes from the contract, and the formula adapts: «в течение срока, предусмотренного пунктом 5.2 договора» (v tee-CHE-nee-ye SRO-ka pre-doos-MOT-ren-na-va POONK-tam pa-TY-tam dva da-ga-VO-ra), 'within the period stipulated in clause 5.2 of the contract'.
lessons.example:
Here is the same claim as a whole letter, then the same facts as a request, then the version learners write. The claim: «Генеральному директору ООО «Север» Соколову А. П. от индивидуального предпринимателя Петровой М. С. Претензия о возврате уплаченной суммы. 12 марта 2026 года мы заключили договор поставки № 14. Оборудование было поставлено с нарушением срока на двадцать дней и с повреждением упаковки. В соответствии со статьёй 31 Закона о защите прав потребителей прошу в течение десяти дней с момента получения настоящей претензии вернуть уплаченную сумму в размере 84 000 рублей. В случае неисполнения обязательств в установленный срок я буду вынуждена обратиться в суд. Приложение: 1. Копия договора. 2. Копия акта приёмки. 3. Копия чека. 20 мая 2026 г. М. С. Петрова.» The subject line is a noun phrase with о plus the prepositional: о возврате, 'about the return'. The facts are perfective past, one action each, no background. The demand carries three things a reader can check: the action, the period, the amount. The consequence is in the first person singular because the claimant is an individual entrepreneur, not a company.

The request letter uses the same layout and none of the accusation: «Уважаемый Андрей Петрович! Обращаюсь к Вам по вопросу графика поставок на второй квартал. Прошу рассмотреть возможность переноса двух поставок с апреля на май. Если это возможно, просим подтвердить новый график до 1 апреля. Буду признателен за ответ. С уважением, М. С. Петрова.» (oo-va-ZHA-ye-my an-DRYEY peet-RO-veech, ab-ra-SHCHA-yus k vam pa vap-RO-soo GRA-fee-ka pas-TA-vak na fta-ROY KVART-al, pra-SHOO ras-sma-TRYET vas-MOZH-nast pee-ree-NO-sa dvookh pas-TA-vak s ap-RYE-lya na may, YES-lee EH-ta vaz-MOZH-na, pra-SEEM pat-peer-DEET NO-vy GRA-feek da pir-VA-va ap-RYE-lya, BOO-doo pree-ZNA-tye-lyen za at-VYET, s oo-va-ZHYE-nee-em), 'Dear Andrei Petrovich, I am writing about the delivery schedule for the second quarter. I ask you to consider moving two deliveries from April to May. If that is possible, please confirm the new schedule by 1 April. I would be grateful for a reply. Yours sincerely, M. S. Petrova.' Nothing here alleges breach, so there is no statute, no deadline imposed on the other side, and no consequence. Note the shift from a singular claim to a plural request only in the phrase просим подтвердить, which reads as the company speaking; mixing я and мы inside one letter is the small inconsistency that makes a Russian reader suspect a template.

Now the learner's version: «Я очень недоволен вашей работой. Вы всё испортили. Требую немедленно всё исправить, иначе я буду жаловаться!» (ya O-chen nee-da-VO-lyen VA-shey ra-BO-tay, vy vsyo ees-POR-tee-lee, TRYE-boo-yoo nee-med-LYEN-na vsyo ees-PRA-veet, ee-NA-che ya BOO-doo ZHA-la-va-tsya), 'I am very dissatisfied with your work. You have ruined everything. I demand that everything be fixed immediately, otherwise I will complain.' It names no contract, no date, no amount and no period, it uses the verb требовать before establishing any right, and it promises a complaint to an unnamed third party. A Russian recipient reads it as emotion rather than as a claim and files it accordingly.
lessons.question: You send a supplier the sentence «Я очень недоволен вашей работой и требую немедленно всё исправить». The supplier does not answer. What was wrong with the letter, and what should replace that sentence?
lessons.answer: It states a feeling rather than a breach, names no contract, no date and no amount, imposes no period, and uses требовать before any right has been established; a claim needs the facts, the basis, the specific demand with a period, and the consequence.
lessons.distractor: Nothing structural; Russian suppliers answer only letters written on company letterhead, so the letter needed a logo rather than a different sentence.
lessons.correction: The letter fails on four counts and each has a repair. Naming a feeling gives the supplier nothing to respond to, because недоволен is not a breach of contract; the repair is a dated fact, «12 марта 2026 года мы заключили договор поставки № 14». Saying «вы всё испортили» identifies no obligation; the repair is the specific term that was broken, «оборудование было поставлено с нарушением срока на двадцать дней». Требовать is a legal verb that presupposes an established right, and using it first makes the writer sound aggressive rather than firm; the standard verb even in a claim is прошу, with firmness carried by the statute and the deadline. And «немедленно» is not a period a court can measure; the repair is «в течение десяти дней с момента получения настоящей претензии». The promised complaint is also misplaced: in a претензия the consequence is court, not a complaint, because a complaint goes to a third party and belongs to a different genre. The corrected core reads: «В соответствии со статьёй 31 Закона о защите прав потребителей прошу в течение десяти дней вернуть уплаченную сумму. В случае неисполнения я буду вынуждена обратиться в суд.»

depth.definitions: Претензия is a formal claim against a party to an agreement, used before litigation and often required by a contract as a precondition of it; the adjective досудебная (da-soo-DYEB-na-ya), 'pre-trial', names that function. Жалоба is a complaint to a body or official with authority over the party at fault. Письмо-просьба is a request with no allegation of wrongdoing. Срок (SROK) is the period within which something must be done, and it is the element that turns a wish into an actionable demand. Неустойка (nee-oos-TOY-ka) is the contractual penalty for delay, a word that belongs in the claim only if the contract provides it. Отметка о получении (at-MYET-ka a pa-loo-CHE-nee-ee), 'mark of receipt', is the date and signature the recipient puts on your copy, which is why a claim is delivered in two copies. Заказное письмо с описью вложения (za-kaz-NO-ye pees-MO s O-pee-syu vla-ZHYE-nee-ya), 'registered letter with an inventory of contents', is the postal form that proves what was sent. Prerequisites: the layout of lesson 121, the register of rules in lesson 92, the message routine of lesson 97, and the fronted phrase and final position of lesson 101.
depth.mechanism: A claim works because each sentence answers a question the recipient will ask in order, and the order is the argument. What was agreed, when, and in what document? What went wrong, and how much? What rule makes that wrong? What must be done, by when? What follows if it is not done? Russian encodes the conditional without a clause: в случае plus the genitive (в случае неисполнения, в случае отказа, в случае повреждения) sets a condition in a noun phrase, which keeps the sentence short and the tone impersonal. The law is quoted in the passive, подлежат удовлетворению, which removes the speaker from the sentence and makes the demand seem to come from the statute. The consequence uses a short adjective with a future copula, буду вынужден, and the feminine form буду вынуждена follows the writer's gender, a detail that marks the letter as written by a person rather than generated from a template. Finally, the demand is fronted: «В соответствии со статьёй 31 ... прошу ...» puts the basis first and прошу second, which is the word-order move of lesson 101, and it produces a sentence that sounds like a document rather than a request.
depth.secondExample: The same facts sent to a regulator become a жалоба, and the verb changes with the addressee. «В Управление Федеральной службы по надзору в сфере защиты прав потребителей. Жалоба на нарушение сроков поставки. 12 марта 2026 года я заключила договор с ООО «Север». Поставка была произведена с нарушением срока на двадцать дней. Моя претензия от 20 мая 2026 года оставлена без ответа. Прошу провести проверку изложенных обстоятельств и сообщить о принятых мерах в письменном виде. Приложение: копия договора, копия претензии, копия ответа.» (v oop-rav-LYE-nee-ye fee-de-RAL-nay SLOOZH-by pa nad-ZO-roo f SFYE-rye za-SHEE-ty praf pa-tree-BEE-tye-lyey, ZHA-la-ba na na-roo-SHYE-nee-ye SRO-kaf pas-TAF-kee, pra-SHOO pra-vees-TEE PRO-vyer-koo eez-LO-zhen-nykh ab-sta-YA-tyel-stv ee sa-ap-SHCHEET a pree-NYA-tykh MYE-rakh v PEES-men-nam VEE-dye), 'to the Federal Service for Supervision of Consumer Rights Protection, complaint about breach of delivery deadlines, I ask that the circumstances set out be investigated and that I be informed in writing of the measures taken'. Three things have changed and nothing else should. The addressee is a body, not the party at fault. The final verb is прошу провести проверку, an investigation, not прошу вернуть, a payment. And the claim you already sent becomes an enclosure and a dated fact, which is why the жалоба mentions it: a regulator wants to see that you tried to settle first. If you send this text to the supplier instead, it is a claim that demands an investigation the supplier has no power to conduct, and it will be read as confused.
depth.mistake: Four errors dominate. The first is genre confusion: a претензия sent to a regulator, or a жалоба sent to the guilty party. Diagnostic: look at the addressee and at the final verb; if the addressee caused the problem, the verb must be a demand for performance, and if the addressee supervises, it must be a request to investigate. The second is требовать without a basis, which in Russian reads as rudeness rather than strength, because the verb names a legal right and presupposes that the right has already been established in the same letter. The third is a demand with no period, or with немедленно, which cannot be measured; every claim needs a date or a number of days counted from a stated event. The fourth is the calque: «Надеюсь на ваше понимание» (na-DYE-yus na VA-she pa-nee-MA-nee-ye), 'I hope for your understanding', translated from a closing formula of English complaints. In Russian it reads as a plea and weakens the letter; the functional equivalents are «Прошу ответить в письменном виде» or «Буду признателен за ответ в указанный срок». A fifth, smaller error is в течении for в течение: the preposition ends in -ее, while the noun in the prepositional case, в течении реки, means 'in the current of the river'.
depth.application: Write one claim about something that actually annoyed you, a late delivery, a wrong item, a service not performed. Draft only the four load-bearing sentences first, facts, breach, basis, demand with a period and a consequence, and check that each one names a document, a date, an amount or a period. Then expand them into a full letter of no more than 180 words, add the subject line as a noun phrase with о plus the prepositional, and number the enclosures. Next, rewrite the same letter as a жалоба to a supervisory body: change the addressee, change the final verb to прошу провести проверку, and turn your own claim into an enclosure. Finally, cut the claim to a three-line email to the supplier's account manager, keeping the amount, the period and the consequence. The three versions together take about thirty minutes and give you a template you can reuse for years.
depth.summary: Претензия, жалоба and письмо-просьба share a layout and differ in addressee and final verb. The claim states dated facts, names the breach, cites the basis with в соответствии с plus the instrumental or на основании plus the genitive, demands a specific action within a period taken from the statute or the contract, and states the consequence with буду вынужден plus an infinitive. The complaint to a third party asks for an investigation. The request alleges nothing. Firmness in Russian comes from the legal reference and the deadline, never from adjectives, and прошу remains the verb of a demand even when the demand is one the other side cannot refuse.

readings.title: КонсультантПлюс, Закон РФ «О защите прав потребителей» от 07.02.1992 № 2300-1
readings.note: Read articles 28 to 31. Article 31 is the source of the ten-day period quoted in this lesson and of the passive formula подлежат удовлетворению в десятидневный срок; article 29 lists the demands a consumer may make when work is defective, which is the list your claim has to choose from. Reading the statute also shows why a claim echoes legal wording instead of inventing its own. Caveat: this is a legal text in a commercial database, it is amended often and the page shows the current edition, so cite the article number rather than copying a sentence, and do not treat it as a writing model.

readings.title: Википедия, «Официально-деловой стиль»
readings.note: Read the section Разновидности, which separates legislative, administrative and diplomatic subtypes, and then the section Примеры, which shows how a clause is written rather than what it means. The distinction matters here because a претензия sits between two subtypes: it is administrative in form and legal in function, and that is why it borrows the statute's phrasing. Caveat: the article is flagged as lacking citations and its examples are short, so use it to orient yourself and take the actual formulas from the statute or from a real letter.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Polite imperatives'
readings.note: Read the whole page, which is short. It explains why the imperfective imperative sounds friendlier than the perfective: the imperfective invites the addressee to start, the perfective tells them to finish, and the page's example is the host's садитесь against the doctor's сядьте. That is the mechanism behind the tone of a request letter, where прошу plus an imperfective infinitive (рассмотреть, подтвердить is perfective, but the frame softens it) keeps the addressee from feeling ordered. Caveat: the page is a 1980s textbook, its Cyrillic is set in a custom font and decodes as garbage, so read the English and do not quote the examples letter by letter.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Business letter'
readings.note: Read the sections on the structure of a business letter and on the opening and closing, then compare with the Russian layout: the English inside address, salutation and complimentary close map onto the Russian header, обращение and формула вежливости, but the cases do not map at all. The comparison is the point, because most learner errors in this genre come from translating an English letter's parts rather than from bad Russian. Caveat: the article describes English-language conventions, chiefly British and American, and says nothing about Russian, so use it as a contrast and not as a source for Russian formulas.

visual.title: Four-sentence claim skeleton with the genre switch at the end
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: four numbered boxes down the page, one per load-bearing sentence, each with the question it answers, the formula that fills it and the case it requires; a fifth box branches into two outcomes, court or investigation, depending on the addressee.
steps: Step 1, draw four boxes. Label them facts, breach, basis, demand. Under box 1 write the question When and what did we agree, and in which document? Under box 2 write What went wrong, and by how much? Under box 3 write Which rule makes that wrong? Under box 4 write What must be done, by when?

Step 2, fill each box with a model. Box 1: 12 марта 2026 года мы заключили договор поставки № 14. Box 2: Оборудование было поставлено с нарушением срока на двадцать дней. Box 3: в соответствии со статьёй 31 Закона о защите прав потребителей. Box 4: прошу в течение десяти дней вернуть уплаченную сумму.

Step 3, mark the case under each preposition. Under box 3 write instrumental after в соответствии с, genitive after на основании. Under box 4 write genitive after в течение and genitive after с момента. These four labels are the grammar content of the whole letter.

Step 4, add the consequence box. Write В случае неисполнения обязательств в установленный срок я буду вынуждена обратиться в суд, and underline the genitive after в случае and the short adjective вынуждена, which agrees with the writer.

Step 5, branch on the addressee. From box 4 draw two arrows. The upper arrow, labelled to the party at fault, keeps прошу вернуть and ends in court. The lower arrow, labelled to a supervisory body, replaces the verb with прошу провести проверку and ends in сообщить о принятых мерах.

Step 6, test the skeleton. Cover everything except boxes 1 to 4 and read them aloud. If a listener can say what was agreed, what broke, which rule applies and what must happen by when, the letter will survive; if any answer is missing, no adjective will supply it.

lessons.title: Email in Russian: the opening and the closing are chosen by the relationship, not by the medium
lessons.explanation:
Russian email has a narrower range than English email, and the range is set by the relationship rather than by the speed of the channel. The opening is an обращение (ab-ra-SHCHE-nee-ye), 'address form', and it stands in the nominative: «Уважаемый Иван Петрович!» (oo-va-ZHA-ye-my ee-VAN peet-RO-veech), 'dear Ivan Petrovich', with the name and patronymic and no surname, or «Уважаемая Анна Сергеевна!» (oo-va-ZHA-ye-ma-YA A-na syer-GYE-yev-na), 'dear Anna Sergeevna'. To a group the form is «Уважаемые коллеги!» (oo-va-ZHA-ye-my-ye kal-LYE-gee), 'dear colleagues', and to a named group «Уважаемые коллеги» still works because the group is the addressee. When the relationship is already established but the register stays polite, «Добрый день, Иван Петрович!» (DO-bry dyen, ee-VAN peet-RO-veech) is the common compromise, and «Здравствуйте!» (ZDRA-stvooy-tye) is the neutral minimum that never offends. The punctuation is a comma or an exclamation mark after the address; the exclamation mark is the older convention and still the default in letters from institutions, while a comma is normal in email between people who have corresponded before.

The failures are specific and learners make the same four. «Уважаемый коллега!» without a name reads as a circular sent to a mailing list, because Russian уважаемый wants a name or a plural noun after it. «Дорогой Иван Петрович!» translates English dear and lands as intimate or ironic, since дорогой in an address is what one writes to a friend, a relative or a lover, and in a business letter it can sound like a reproach. «Господин Иванов!» is business-formal in the post-Soviet press and in translated contracts, but in an ordinary email from one professional to another it sets a distance that Russians often read as coldness or sarcasm. And «Здравствуйте, Иван!» mixes a formal greeting with a bare first name, which signals that the writer is not sure whether the relationship is ты or вы; lesson 78 showed that the pronoun and the verb ending must agree, and the address form is part of the same choice.

The closing is a formula, not a sentence, and it marks the relationship as clearly as the opening. «С уважением,» (s oo-va-ZHYE-nee-em) followed by the name on the next line is the default for anybody you call вы, from a stranger to your director, and it is written with a comma and no full stop after the name. «С наилучшими пожеланиями,» (s na-eel-LOOT-shee-mee pa-zhe-LA-nee-ya-mee), 'with best wishes', is warmer and belongs to people you have met. «Всего доброго,» (fsy-VO DO-bra-va), 'all the best', is friendly and slightly informal, acceptable to a colleague and too light for a first contact with an institution. «До свидания» is a farewell in speech or at the end of a telephone call, never a letter closing, and a bare «Спасибо!» at the end of a request reads as an instruction to comply rather than as a sign-off. The signature block carries what the letterhead would carry in a paper letter: name, position, organisation, telephone, and in a student's email the group number.
lessons.example:
Three emails, three relationships. To an official you have never met: «Уважаемая Ирина Викторовна! Меня зовут Мария Соколова, я студентка второго курса исторического факультета, группа 2-14. В ответ на Ваше письмо от 12 мая направляю копию справки об обучении. Подскажите, пожалуйста, нужно ли представить оригинал до конца месяца. С уважением, Мария Соколова, группа 2-14, телефон +7 900 000 00 00.» (oo-va-ZHA-ye-ma-YA ee-REE-na veek-TA-rav-na, mee-NYA za-VOOT ma-REE-ya sa-ka-LO-va, ya stoo-DYENT-ka fta-RO-va KOR-sa ees-ta-REE-ches-ka-va fa-kool-TYE-ta GROO-pa dveh chee-TYR-na-tsat, v at-VYET na VA-she pees-MO at dvee-NA-tsa-ta-va MA-ya nap-rav-LYA-yoo KO-pee-yu SPRAF-kee ab oo-CHE-nee-ee, pat-SKA-zhee-tye pa-ZHA-loos-ta, NOOZH-na lee preet-STA-veet a-ree-gee-NAL da kants-TSA MYE-sya-tsa, s oo-va-ZHYE-nee-em), 'Dear Irina Viktorovna, my name is Maria Sokolova, I am a second-year student of the history faculty, group 2-14. In reply to your letter of 12 May I am sending a copy of my certificate of enrolment. Please tell me whether the original has to be submitted before the end of the month. Yours sincerely, Maria Sokolova, group 2-14, telephone ...'. Five moves in eight lines: address, self-identification, reference to the previous letter, the substance, one question with пожалуйста, closing formula and signature block.

To a colleague you call ты, the same content and a different channel: «Привет, Олег! Спасибо за файл, всё открылось. Скинь, пожалуйста, ещё смету за апрель, если она у тебя есть. До завтра!» (pree-VYET, a-LYEK, spa-SEE-ba za fyle, vsyo at-KRY-la-s, skeen pa-ZHA-loos-ta yeshch SMYE-too za ap-RYEL, YES-lee a-NA oo tee-BYA yest, da ZAF-tra), 'Hi Oleg, thanks for the file, it opened fine. Send me the April estimate too, please, if you have it. See you tomorrow.' Imperatives in the ты form, a bare thanks, a farewell, no formula at all. This is not a degraded version of the first email; it is the correct version for the relationship, and using «С уважением» here would signal that something is wrong.

To a group, where the addressee is plural and nobody is named: «Уважаемые коллеги! Напоминаю, что совещание по проекту переносится на 15 мая, 11:00, кабинет 312. Прошу подтвердить участие до 13 мая. С уважением, Мария Соколова.» (oo-va-ZHA-ye-my-ye kal-LYE-gee, na-pee-mee-NA-yoo, shto sa-vee-SHCHA-nee-ye pa pra-YEK-too pee-ree-NO-seet-sya na peet-NA-tsa-ta-ye MA-ya, a-dee-NA-tsat cha-SOF, ka-bee-NYET TREE-sta dvee-NA-tsat, pra-SHOO pat-peer-DEET oo-CHA-stee-ye da tree-NA-tsa-ta-va MA-ya), 'Dear colleagues, I remind you that the project meeting is moved to 15 May, 11:00, room 312. Please confirm attendance by 13 May. Yours sincerely, Maria Sokolova.' Note that the closing formula stays even though the greeting is plural, and that the request is a finite прошу with an infinitive, the same frame as a заявление.

Now the version that fails: «Дорогой господин Иванов! Надеюсь, у вас всё хорошо. Я хочу спросить про справку. Спасибо!» (da-ra-GOY gas-pa-DEEN ee-VA-noff, na-DYE-yus, oo vas vsyo ha-ra-SHO, ya kha-CHOO spra-SEET pra SPRAF-koo, spa-SEE-ba), 'Dear Mr Ivanov, I hope all is well with you. I want to ask about the certificate. Thanks.' Every sentence is grammatical, and the message breaks four conventions at once: дорогой господин is a translated greeting that Russians read as either intimate or mocking, «надеюсь, у вас всё хорошо» is small talk that has no place in a first contact with an office, «я хочу спросить» describes the wish instead of making the request, and «Спасибо!» closes a message that has not yet been answered.
lessons.question: You write to a university office you have never contacted: «Привет! Меня зовут Мария, я хочу спросить про справку. Спасибо!» What must change, and what stays?
lessons.answer: The greeting becomes «Здравствуйте!» or «Добрый день!», the self-identification moves to a full name with group and faculty, the request becomes a формула («Подскажите, пожалуйста, ...» or «Прошу сообщить ...»), and the close becomes «С уважением, Мария Соколова, группа 2-14»; the content of the question stays exactly as it is.
lessons.distractor: Only the word Привет needs replacing; the rest is fine, because email is an informal medium and the office will read the question anyway.
lessons.correction: The register of an email is fixed by the relationship, not by the medium, so changing one word changes nothing. Привет is a ты greeting and it presupposes that the reader knows who you are, which the office does not; «Меня зовут Мария» is a face-to-face or telephone formula, because in writing the signature does the identifying, and a Russian official needs a surname and a group or department to find your file. «Я хочу спросить» reports an intention where the genre expects the question itself or a request frame, and a bare «Спасибо!» thanks somebody for an answer they have not given, which is why it reads as pressure. The repair is not to make the message longer but to move each piece into its slot: greeting, identification, one sentence of context, one question with пожалуйста, closing formula, signature block. The substance, that you need a certificate, is the part that stays untouched, which is the useful lesson: register is a frame around content, and the content survives the frame change intact.

depth.definitions: Обращение (ab-ra-SHCHE-nee-ye) is the address form, a noun phrase in the nominative set off by a comma or an exclamation mark, and it is not part of the sentence that follows. Формула вежливости (FOR-moo-la vyezh-LEE-vas-tee), 'politeness formula', is a fixed closing or opening with no verb of its own, such as с уважением or всего доброго; its job is relational rather than propositional. Тема письма (TYE-ma pees-MA) is the subject line, which in Russian official email is a noun phrase, often with о plus the prepositional, as in О переносе совещания, 'on the postponement of the meeting'. Подпись (POD-pees) in email means the signature block rather than a handwritten signature, and it carries the information a paper letterhead would carry. Деловая переписка (dee-la-VA-ya pee-REES-ka) is business correspondence as a genre. Prerequisites: the ты and вы channels of lesson 78, the written politeness of lesson 97, the letter layout of lesson 121, and the particles of lesson 102, which are exactly what must not appear in this register.
depth.mechanism: The Russian address form encodes two variables at once, distance and gender, and the patronymic is the mechanism that carries distance. A name plus patronymic says that the writer acknowledges the addressee's adult, official identity and keeps the relationship at вы; a bare first name claims the intimacy of ты; a bare surname claims institutional distance or, in a letter, rudeness. That is why «Уважаемый Иван» sounds wrong rather than merely informal: it pairs the most formal adjective in the set with the most intimate noun form, and the reader cannot tell which relationship is being proposed. The closing works the other way round. It has no content, so its only function is to name the relationship at the end, which is why «С уважением» can close a message to a stranger and cannot close a message to a friend without irony. Email adds one constraint that paper letters do not have: there is no letterhead to identify the sender, so the subject line and the signature block take over the header's work from lesson 121, and an email without them leaves the reader unable to file it.
depth.secondExample: Two email moves that learners rarely practise, a refusal and a chase-up. Refusal: «Уважаемая Ольга Петровна! Спасибо за приглашение. К сожалению, я не смогу участвовать в совещании 15 мая, потому что в этот день у меня защита курсовой работы. Предлагаю обсудить вопросы проекта 16 мая после обеда. С уважением, Мария Соколова.» (spa-SEE-ba za pree-gla-SHYE-nee-ye, k sa-zha-LYE-nee-yu, ya ne sma-GOO oo-CHA-stva-vat f sa-vee-SHCHA-nee-ee peet-NA-tsa-ta-va MA-ya, pa-ta-MOO shto v EH-tat dyen oo mee-NYA za-SHCHEE-ta koor-sa-VOY ra-BO-ty, pred-la-GA-yu ab-soo-DEET vap-RO-sy pra-YEK-ta shyes-NA-tsa-ta-va MA-ya POS-lye a-BYE-da), 'Dear Olga Petrovna, thank you for the invitation. Unfortunately I will not be able to take part in the meeting on 15 May, because on that day I have my coursework defence. I suggest discussing the project questions on 16 May after lunch. Yours sincerely, Maria Sokolova.' The refusal is done in three moves: thanks, inability with a reason, and an alternative, which is the same repair sequence that lesson 87 taught for spoken disagreement, transferred to writing without the particles. Chase-up: «Уважаемый Игорь Анатольевич! Повторно направляю Вам запрос от 5 мая о сроках поставки. Прошу ответить до 20 мая. С уважением, Мария Соколова.» (pat-TOR-na nap-rav-LYA-yoo vam za-PROS at PYA-ta-va MA-ya a SRO-kakh pas-TAF-kee, pra-SHOO at-VYE-teet da dvee-tsa-ta-va MA-ya), 'Dear Igor Anatolyevich, I am sending you again the request of 5 May about delivery dates. Please reply by 20 May.' Повторно is the word that makes a chase-up polite: it records the earlier attempt without accusing anybody, which a phrase like «вы не отвечаете» would do.
depth.mistake: Five errors recur. The first is translating dear as дорогой, which in an address means intimate or ironic. The second is «Уважаемый» with a bare first name, which mixes the two channels; the repair is either name plus patronymic or a bare «Здравствуйте». The third is «До свидания» as a closing, which belongs to a call or a meeting, not to a letter; the written equivalents are с уважением and всего доброго. The fourth is a missing subject line, or a sentence in the subject line, as in «Я хочу спросить про справку»; Russian official email wants a noun phrase, «Справка об обучении», or о plus the prepositional. The fifth is mixing the channels inside one message, for example «Здравствуйте! Отправь, пожалуйста, файл», where the greeting is вы and the imperative is ты; lesson 78 established that the pronoun and the ending agree, and the same rule governs the address form. Diagnostic for all five: read only the first line and the last two lines and ask what relationship they describe; if the answer differs between the top and the bottom of the message, one of them is wrong.
depth.application: Write three emails of the same length about the same fact, a document you need from an office. The first goes to an official you have never met, the second to a colleague you call вы but have worked with for years, the third to a colleague you call ты. Use the full frame in the first, the compromise «Добрый день, имя отчество» in the second, and the bare Привет with a ты imperative in the third. Then do the swap test: take the opening of one and the closing of another and read the hybrid aloud; if the hybrid sounds absurd, you have understood that the opening and the closing are one choice, not two. Finally, write the subject line for each of the three as a noun phrase and check that it names the object, not the action: «Справка об обучении» rather than «Нужна справка». Twenty minutes, and keep the three versions as templates, because the next email you send will be one of these three relationships.
depth.summary: Russian email is a letter with the letterhead removed. The opening is an address in the nominative, name plus patronymic for вы, a bare name for ты, «Уважаемые коллеги» for a group, and «Здравствуйте» as the neutral floor. The closing is a formula, «С уважением» by default, «С наилучшими пожеланиями» for people you have met, «Всего доброго» for colleagues, and never «До свидания». The subject line is a noun phrase and does the filing work, and the signature block does the identifying work. The medium is fast; the relationship is what chooses the words.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Addressing people: ty vs. vy'
readings.note: Read the whole page. It sets out the two channels, the singular ты and the plural or polite вы, and the rule that the verb agrees with the pronoun chosen, which is the grammar underneath this lesson's address forms. The page also notes the asymmetry that a stranger may address you as ты while you answer with вы, a situation you will meet in a Russian office and should recognise rather than imitate. Caveat: the page is a 1980s textbook, its Cyrillic is rendered in a custom font and decodes as gibberish, so read the English prose and take the Russian forms from the item list here.

The article describes the Russian business encounter as a sequence of fixed moves, and that sequence is what an email compresses into an opening and a closing: greeting, identification, exchange of the minimum personal information, then business. Read it for the inventory of moves rather than for email advice. Caveat: this is an encyclopedia article with uneven sourcing and a good deal of general etiquette material that is not specifically Russian, so check any particular claim against a Russian source before you rely on it.

readings.note: Read the sections Особенности and Разновидности. The features listed there, standardised formulas, absence of emotional vocabulary, preference for nominal phrases, are exactly the features that make a Russian email to an institution sound the way it does, and they explain why «надеюсь, у вас всё хорошо» is out of place. readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Business letter'

The mapping is the useful exercise and also the warning: English 'Dear Mr Ivanov' has no Russian equivalent that is safe in both directions, and English 'Yours sincerely' corresponds to с уважением only in function, not in warmth. visual.title: Relationship ladder: four addressees, four openings, four closings
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: a vertical ladder with four rungs, each rung naming a relationship, the pronoun that goes with it, the opening that fits and the closing that fits, plus a red margin column listing the forms that break the pairing.
steps: Step 1, draw four rungs and label them from the top: stranger in an institution, official you deal with regularly, colleague you call вы, colleague you call ты. Write the pronoun beside each: вы, вы, вы, ты.

Step 2, fill the opening column. Top rung: Уважаемая Ирина Викторовна! Second: Добрый день, Ирина Викторовна! Third: Здравствуйте, Ирина! Fourth: Привет, Ира! Note that only the top rung requires the patronymic, and that the third rung keeps the вы verb forms even though the name is bare.

Step 3, fill the closing column. Top: С уважением, plus имя и фамилия, plus group or position and telephone. Second: С уважением or С наилучшими пожеланиями. Third: Всего доброго. Fourth: До завтра or Пока, with no formula.

Step 4, fill the subject-line column. Every rung except the last needs a noun phrase: Справка об обучении, Перенос совещания, Счёт за апрель. On the bottom rung the subject line can be omitted or reduced to one word.

Step 5, write the margin column. List the forms that break the ladder: Дорогой господин, Уважаемый коллега without a name, Уважаемый Иван, До свидания as a closing, and Здравствуйте with a ты imperative. Beside each, write which two rungs it tries to combine.

Step 6, test a real message. Take an email you have sent and place it on the ladder. If the opening and the closing sit on different rungs, the message is describing two relationships at once, and the reader will believe the colder of the two.

lessons.title: On the telephone: identification, request and repair, in the formulas Russian actually uses
lessons.explanation:
The telephone removes the visual channel, so each call has to rebuild in words what a meeting supplies by presence: who is speaking, whom they want, and why. Russian has fixed formulas for each of those steps, and a call built from them sounds competent even when the grammar is simple. The receiver's first word is «Алло!» (a-LO), which is neutral and works in every setting, or a bare «Да!» (DA), which is shorter and slightly curt. An institution answers with its own name and a greeting: «Компания «Север», добрый день!» (kam-PA-nee-ya SYE-veer, DO-bry DYEN), 'Sever company, good afternoon'. The terse «Слушаю» (SLOO-sha-yoo), literally 'I am listening', is what a busy official says, and learners should recognise it rather than copy it, because from a subordinate it reads as impatience.

Identification is where the formulas are most specific. «Это Иван Петров» (EH-ta ee-VAN peet-ROF), 'this is Ivan Petrov', is the neutral form; это here is presentational and does not refer to anything, which is why «Я Иван» sounds like a translation. When the call is unexpected or the addressee is senior, the polite form is «Вас беспокоит Иван Петров» (vas bees-pa-KO-eet ee-VAN peet-ROF), literally 'Ivan Petrov is troubling you', and the verb беспокоить takes the accusative because the caller acknowledges the imposition. «Меня зовут Иван» belongs to a face-to-face introduction and sounds strange on the telephone, where the other person cannot see you and needs a surname and an organisation instead. If the call is a follow-up to a letter, the identification includes the reference: «Я звоню по поводу письма от 12 мая» (ya zva-NYOO pa PA-va-doo pees-MA at dvee-NA-tsa-ta-va MA-ya), 'I am calling about the letter of 12 May'.

Asking for a person has two frames. «Можно Сергея Петровича?» (MOZH-na syer-GYE-ya peet-RO-vee-cha), 'may I speak to Sergei Petrovich?', puts the name in the accusative because it is the object of an omitted попросить or пригласить; the frame is elliptical and that is why the case looks unmotivated. «Соедините, пожалуйста, с Сергеем Петровичем» (sa-ee-dee-NEE-tye pa-ZHA-loos-ta s syer-GYE-yem peet-RO-vee-chem) uses the imperative with с plus the instrumental, and it is the form to use with a switchboard. Extensions take the same frame: «Добавочный 214, пожалуйста» (da-BA-vach-ny DVA-sya-chee chye-TYR-na-tsat), 'extension 214, please'. Asking who is on the line has a polite and a curt version: «Простите, с кем я говорю?» (pras-TEE-tye, s kyem ya ga-va-RYOO), 'excuse me, whom am I speaking to?', and the secretary's «Кто его спрашивает?» (kto ee-VO SPRA-shee-va-yet), 'who is asking for him?', which is not rude in a Russian office but is an instruction to identify yourself.

Repair is the third skill, and the phrases are short. «Минуту, пожалуйста» (mee-NOO-too pa-ZHA-loos-ta) or «Одну секунду» (ad-NOO see-KOON-doo) asks for time. «Вас не слышно» (vas ne SLYSH-na), 'you cannot be heard', and «Связь прерывается» (SVYAS pree-ree-VA-yet-sya), 'the connection keeps breaking', describe the line rather than blaming the person. «Перезвоните, пожалуйста» (pee-reez-va-NEE-tye pa-ZHA-loos-ta), 'please call back', and «Я вам перезвоню» (ya vam pee-reez-va-NYOO), 'I will call you back', are the two directions of the same repair, and both take the dative of the person, which is the case that lesson 61 gave to the recipient of a call. The verb дозвониться (da-zva-NEET-sya), 'to get through', exists only with до plus the genitive: «Я не могу дозвониться до вас» (ya ne ma-GOO da-zva-NEET-sya da vas), 'I cannot get through to you'.
lessons.example:
A complete call to a clinic, with every slot filled. «Алло, поликлиника номер пять, добрый день.» «Здравствуйте, вас беспокоит Мария Соколова. Я звоню по поводу записи к кардиологу.» «Минуту, пожалуйста, я посмотрю.» «Спасибо.» «Ваша запись на 14 мая, в десять тридцать.» «Простите, с кем я говорю?» «Это администратор, Ольга Ивановна.» «Ольга Ивановна, можно перенести запись на 20 мая?» «Можно, но только на утро.» «Тогда на 20 мая, на девять утра, если это возможно.» «Записали.» «Спасибо большое, всего доброго.» (a-LO, pa-lee-KLEE-nee-ka NO-mer pyat, DO-bry DYEN, ZDRA-stvooy-tye, vas bees-pa-KO-eet ma-REE-ya sa-ka-LO-va, ya zva-NYOO pa PA-va-doo ZA-pee-see k kar-dee-O-la-goo, mee-NOO-too pa-ZHA-loos-ta, ya pas-mat-RYOO, spa-SEE-ba, VA-sha ZA-pees na chye-TYR-na-tsa-ta-ye MA-ya, f DYE-syat TREE-tsat, pras-TEE-tye, s kyem ya ga-va-RYOO, EH-ta ad-mee-nees-TRA-tar, OL-ga ee-VA-nav-na, OL-ga ee-VA-nav-na, MOZH-na pee-ree-nees-TEE ZA-pees na dvee-tsa-ta-ye MA-ya, MOZH-na, no TOL-ka na OOT-ra, ta-GDA na dvee-tsa-ta-ye MA-ya, NA dev-yat OOT-ra, YES-lee EH-ta vaz-MOZH-na, za-pee-SA-lee, spa-SEE-ba bal-SHO-ye, fsy-VO DO-bra-va). Look at what the caller never says. She never says «я хочу» or «мне нужно», because a call is a sequence of requests in the можно frame and of confirmations. She identifies herself with вас беспокоит rather than с an introduction. She asks who she is speaking to with the full polite formula, and she repeats the name and patronymic she is given before making the request, which is the telephone equivalent of turning towards the person you are addressing. And she closes with спасибо plus всего доброго rather than with the bare до свидания that a learner often appends to every call.

The receiving side has its own four moves: «Кто его спрашивает?» (kto ee-VO SPRA-shee-va-yet), 'who is asking for him?'; «Он на совещании» (on na sa-vee-SHCHA-nee-ee), 'he is in a meeting'; «Что ему передать?» (shto ee-MOO pee-ree-DAT), 'what should I pass on to him?'; and «Продиктуйте, пожалуйста, ваш номер» (pra-deek-TOOY-tye pa-ZHA-loos-ta vash NO-mer), 'please dictate your number'. Note the dative in ему and the accusative in ваш номер, and note that передать takes the dative of the recipient and the accusative of the message.
lessons.question: You call a company and say «Я Иван. Мне нужно Сергей Петрович.» The secretary answers «Кто его спрашивает?» and the call goes badly. What should you have said?
lessons.answer: «Здравствуйте, вас беспокоит Иван Петров, компания «Север». Можно Сергея Петровича?» The identification needs это or вас беспокоит plus a surname, and asking for a person takes можно plus the accusative, not нужно plus the nominative.
lessons.distractor: Only the first name was insufficient; «мне нужно Сергей Петрович» is the normal way to ask for somebody on the telephone and the secretary was simply unhelpful.
lessons.correction: Three separate problems produced the bad call. «Я Иван» is a calque of the English pattern and drops the presentational это that Russian requires, so the sentence sounds like a statement about the speaker rather than an identification. A bare first name gives the secretary nothing to search for: Russian offices work with surname, organisation and sometimes patronymic, and «Кто его спрашивает?» is precisely the request for that information. And «мне нужно Сергей Петрович» is grammatical but says that the caller needs this person for a task, which is a statement about the caller's business rather than a request to be connected; the telephone frame is «Можно Сергея Петровича?» with the accusative, an ellipsis of можно попросить, or «Соедините, пожалуйста, с Сергеем Петровичем» with с plus the instrumental. The repaired opening does all three jobs in one breath: greeting, identification with surname and company, and the request in the можно frame. The secretary's question then has an answer already in her hand, and the call proceeds.

depth.definitions: Алло is the telephone answer, borrowed from French and used only on the phone; it is not a greeting and cannot open a letter. Беспокоить (bees-pa-KO-eet) means 'to trouble, to disturb', and in the formula вас беспокоит it is a conventional apology for the interruption rather than a literal one. Соединить (sa-ee-dee-NEET) means 'to connect', used of a switchboard and constructed with с plus the instrumental. Добавочный (da-BA-vach-ny) is an extension number, a noun made from an adjective. Дозвониться до plus the genitive means 'to get through to', and the verb has no other government. Абонент (a-ba-NENT) is a subscriber or account holder, the word a call centre uses for the person on the line. Автоответчик (af-ta-at-VYET-cheek) is an answering machine or voicemail. Prerequisites: the dative recipient of lesson 61, the instrumental after с in lesson 63, the imperatives and their politeness of lesson 69, the aspect pairs of lesson 56, and the register choices of lesson 123.
depth.mechanism: Telephone Russian is fixed because the channel has no shared context. In a meeting, pointing and eye contact identify people; on the phone, every identification must be spoken and every request must name its object, so the language develops short formulas that do both at once. «Вас беспокоит» is the most instructive of them: it puts the listener in the accusative, which makes the listener the object of the caller's action, and it names that action as an interruption, which pre-empts the annoyance the call may cause. «Это» in «это Иван» is a presentational particle rather than a pronoun: it points at the speaker's voice and has no antecedent, which is why replacing it with я changes the meaning from identification to autobiography. The можно frame is an ellipsis, and the accusative of the name is the trace of the missing infinitive попросить or пригласить; because the case survives the ellipsis, the phrase looks irregular until you restore the verb. Aspect does the rest: «перезвоните» is perfective because the callback is one event, while «звоните мне каждый день» is imperfective because the calls repeat, the same contrast lesson 57 established for the present tense.
depth.secondExample: A call in the other direction, where you are the one answering and the caller is a stranger. «Компания «Север», добрый день.» «Здравствуйте, это Анна Крылова, я звоню по объявлению о вакансии.» «Простите, с кем я говорю?» «Анна Крылова, по объявлению.» «Анна, вы можете перезвонить через час? Сейчас идёт совещание.» «Конечно, я перезвоню. На какой номер?» «Продиктуйте, пожалуйста, ваш номер, и я передам, чтобы вам перезвонили.» (kam-PA-nee-ya SYE-veer, DO-bry DYEN, ZDRA-stvooy-tye, EH-ta A-na KRY-la-va, ya zva-NYOO pa ab-yav-LYE-nee-yu a va-KAN-see-ee, pras-TEE-tye, s kyem ya ga-va-RYOO, A-na KRY-la-va, pa ab-yav-LYE-nee-yu, A-na, vy MO-zhe-tye pee-reez-va-NEET chye-ryez chas, see-CHAS ee-DYOT sa-vee-SHCHA-nee-ye, ka-NYESH-na, ya pee-reez-va-NYOO, na ka-KOY NO-mer, pra-deek-TOOY-tye pa-ZHA-loos-ta vash NO-mer, ee ya pee-ree-DAM, SHTO-by vam pee-reez-va-NEE-lee). Four observations. The receiver identifies the company, not herself, because the company is what the caller needs to know. The caller's second identification repeats her surname rather than adding a patronymic, because she is not yet in a вы relationship with this person and a full patronymic would claim more distance than the situation has. «Вы можете перезвонить» is the request for a callback in the вы form with the modal verb, softer than the imperative перезвоните, and it is the form used when the other person has a choice. And the last line uses чтобы plus the past tense, чтобы вам перезвонили, 'so that they call you back', because the subject of the callback is not the speaker; lesson 74 established that чтобы takes the past form when the subjects differ, and the telephone makes that structure routine.
depth.mistake: Five errors recur. The first is «Я есть Иван» or «Я Иван» for identification, where Russian wants это or вас беспокоит. The second is «Алло, кто это?» used as a challenge; it is grammatical but reads as suspicious, and the polite version is «Простите, с кем я говорю?». The third is the case after звонить: the verb takes the dative, so «позвоните мне», not «позвоните меня», and the same dative appears in я вам перезвоню and я ему передам. The fourth is using «Слушаю» when answering a superior or a client, where the institutional terseness sounds like impatience; the neutral answer is алло or the company name plus a greeting. The fifth is starting a call without identifying yourself and asking «А кто это?» only after the other person has spoken, which in a Russian office is treated as a small breach of procedure. Diagnostic for all five: write the first fifteen seconds of the call as a script and check that it contains a greeting, an identification with a surname, the object of the call, and the frame of the request. If any of the four is missing, the secretary will ask for it, and the call will take twice as long.
depth.application: Write a ninety-second call script with six labelled slots: answer, identification, purpose, request, repair, closing. Record yourself performing it with a partner who plays the switchboard and who is instructed to ask «Кто его спрашивает?» and «Что ему передать?» at least once. Then listen to the recording and mark three things: every verb that governs a case you had to think about, every place where you said я where the formula wanted это or вас, and the moment you closed the call. Re-record with the corrections. Next, write the same call in the ты form for a colleague and notice which formulas disappear entirely: вас беспокоит, можно, разрешите, and the closing всего доброго all drop out, while the case government of звонить and перезвонить stays. That comparison is the lesson, because it shows which parts of the telephone genre are politeness and which are grammar.
depth.summary: A Russian call is four moves in a fixed order: answer, identify, state the purpose, request. Алло or the company name answers; это plus a name or вас беспокоит plus a surname identifies; я звоню по поводу plus the genitive states the purpose; можно plus the accusative, or соедините с plus the instrumental, makes the request. Repair is short and blames the line rather than the person: вас не слышно, связь прерывается, перезвоните. Звонить and перезвонить take the dative, дозвониться takes до plus the genitive, and the aspect of the imperative says whether the callback is one event or a habit.

The first section is the general background for this lesson, the second explains why вас беспокоит exists as an apology. readings.title: Википедия, «Деловой этикет»
readings.note: Read the sections on greeting and on the business conversation. They describe the Russian office encounter as a sequence with a fixed opening, and the telephone is the same sequence without the visual part, which is why the call has to say aloud what a meeting shows. Caveat: the article is unevenly sourced and contains a good deal of general etiquette advice that is not specific to Russia, so treat it as a description of conventions rather than as a rule book.

visual.title: Six-slot call script with the case government written under each slot
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: six boxes in the order of a call, each with the Russian formula, the case it requires and the mistake it prevents; a side branch for repair phrases and a second side branch for the receiving side.
steps: Step 1, draw the main line of six boxes: answer, identify, purpose, request, confirm, close. Put the model formula in each: Алло or the company name; вас беспокоит plus имя и фамилия; я звоню по поводу plus genitive; можно plus accusative, or соедините с plus instrumental; спасибо, значит, договорились; всего доброго.

Step 2, label the cases under boxes 3, 4 and 6. Under box 3 write genitive after по поводу. Under box 4 write accusative for the ellipsis with можно, instrumental after с. Under box 6 write nothing, and note that the closing formula has no case government because it has no object.

Step 3, add the repair branch under box 4. Three lines: вас не слышно, связь прерывается, перезвоните, пожалуйста. Beside each write what it blames, the line, the line, and the other person's schedule, because blaming the line is the politeness strategy of this branch.

Step 4, add the receiving branch to the left of box 2. Four lines: кто его спрашивает, он на совещании, что ему передать, продиктуйте ваш номер. Mark the dative in ему and the accusative in ваш номер.
Step 5, mark the aspect choice in the repair branch. Write перезвоните as perfective, one callback, and звоните as imperfective, repeated calls, and add the imperative pair to the margin.

Step 6, run the script. Read the six boxes aloud in order with a partner who interrupts at box 4 with кто его спрашивает. If you can answer inside the script without inventing a sentence, the slots are learned; if you have to translate from English, the slot that stopped you is the one to drill.
