lessons.title: Asking without imposing, and unpacking the noun: the polite request and the register ladder
lessons.explanation:
Russian has a small set of request frames and each one measures a different distance. The most polite is «Не могли бы вы ...?» plus the infinitive: «Не могли бы вы направить счёт повторно?» (nee mag-LEE by vy nap-RA-veet shchyot fta-REEch-na), 'could you send the invoice again?'. The negative is not a denial of ability; with бы it turns the request into a hypothesis, which gives the addressee a grammatical way to decline, and that is exactly what makes it polite. One step down is the можно frame: «Можно попросить вас подписать здесь?» (MOZH-na pa-pra-SEET vas pat-pee-SAT zdyes), 'may I ask you to sign here?', with the person in the accusative, or the elliptical «Можно счёт?» (MOZH-na shchyot), 'may I have the invoice?', which works in a café and in an office. «Будьте добры, ...» (BOOT-tye dab-RY), 'be so kind', takes an imperative and belongs to institutions and to older speakers: «Будьте добры, продиктуйте номер договора» (BOOT-tye dab-RY, pra-deek-TOOY-tye NO-mer da-ga-VO-ra). «Разрешите ...» and «Позвольте ...» (raz-ree-SHEE-tye, paz-VOL-tye) plus the infinitive ask permission rather than action, and they are bookish: «Разрешите задать вопрос» (raz-ree-SHEE-tye za-DAT vap-ROS), 'allow me to ask a question'. The noun frame «У меня к вам просьба» (oo mee-NYA k vam PROS-ba), 'I have a request for you', introduces the request as a thing rather than an action, and «Прошу» plus the infinitive is the document frame of lesson 121.

These frames are not interchangeable, and the choice is governed by two variables: whether the addressee can refuse, and whether the speaker has the right to ask. «Не могли бы вы» presumes the addressee may refuse and is therefore the safest with a stranger or a superior. «Будьте добры» presumes the request is small and routine, which is why it works at a counter and sounds odd when you are asking for a favour. «Разрешите» presumes the speaker needs permission, so it fits entering a room or taking the floor, not asking for a document. «Прошу» presumes an institution and a file. Learners who stack the frames, «Не могли бы Вы, если Вас не затруднит, возможно, рассмотреть нашу просьбу», produce a sentence in which the request has been buried under three hedges, and the reader cannot tell what is being asked or by when.

The second half of this lesson is the opposite problem: official Russian takes the verb out of the sentence and puts a noun in its place. Compare «проверить» (pra-VYE-reet), 'to check', with «проверка» (pra-VYER-ka), 'a check'; «исполнить» with «исполнение» (ees-pal-NYE-nee-ye), 'performance'; «предоставить» with «предоставление» (pree-das-tav-LYE-nee-ye), 'provision'. Each noun keeps its verb's object in the genitive, and the noun phrase can then become the object of another verb, which allows another noun phrase inside it. That recursion produces the chains that make a Russian regulation hard to read: «в целях обеспечения своевременного исполнения обязательств» (f TSE-lyakh ab-yes-PYE-chee-nee-ya svye-ef-ree-MYEN-na-va ees-pal-NYE-nee-ya a-bya-ZA-tyel-stv), 'in order to ensure the timely performance of obligations'. Unpacking is a mechanical operation with three steps. Find each verbal noun, restore the verb it came from, and give that verb a subject. «Обеспечение исполнения» becomes «сделать так, чтобы обязательства были исполнены»; «исполнение обязательств» becomes «обязательства исполняются»; and the whole phrase becomes «чтобы обязательства исполнили в срок». Lesson 85 established that a verbal noun compresses a clause; this lesson runs the compression backwards.
lessons.example:
One request at three rungs of the ladder, all addressed to the same accountant. The bureaucratic rung: «В связи с отсутствием возможности осуществления оплаты в установленный договором срок прошу рассмотреть вопрос о предоставлении отсрочки.» (v SVYA-zee s at-SOOT-stvee-em vaz-MOZH-nas-tee a-soosh-chest-VLYE-nee-ya ap-LA-ty v oo-sta-NOV-lyen-ny da-ga-VO-rom SROK pra-SHOO ras-sma-TRYET vap-ROS a pre-das-tav-LYE-nee-ee at-SROCH-kee), 'in connection with the absence of the possibility of making payment within the period set by the contract, I ask that the question of granting a deferral be considered'. The neutral rung: «Я не смог оплатить счёт в срок, указанный в договоре. Прошу предоставить отсрочку.» (ya ne smog ap-la-TEET shchyot f SROK oo-KA-zan-ny da-ga-VO-re, pra-SHOO pree-das-TA-veet at-SROCH-koo), 'I could not pay the invoice within the period stated in the contract. I ask that a deferral be granted.' The plain rung: «Не успел оплатить счёт. Можно отсрочку на неделю?» (ne oos-PYEL ap-la-TEET shchyot, MOZH-na at-SROCH-koo na nee-DYE-lyu), 'I did not manage to pay the invoice. May I have a deferral for a week?' All three say the same thing, and only the first hides who failed to pay.

Now dissect the bureaucratic sentence. It contains five verbal nouns: отсутствие возможности, осуществление, оплата, предоставление, отсрочка, and one of them, отсутствие, is not even a verbal noun but an abstract one. The actor has disappeared: nobody is named as the payer, and the phrase «в связи с отсутствием возможности» presents the failure as a circumstance rather than an act. The tense has disappeared too, because a noun has no tense, so the reader cannot tell whether the payment is late, impossible or merely uncertain. Unpacking restores all three: «Я не смог оплатить счёт в срок» names the actor in я, restores the verb оплатить, and puts the failure in the past. That is why the neutral rung reads as more honest, and why officials sometimes prefer the first.

Politeness can also fail in the other direction, by stacking. «Не могли бы Вы, если Вас не затруднит, возможно, рассмотреть нашу просьбу о предоставлении отсрочки?» (nee mag-LEE by vy, YES-lee vas ne za-trood-NEET, vaz-MOZH-na, ras-sma-TRYET NA-shoo PROS-boo a pre-das-tav-LYE-nee-ee at-SROCH-kee) has three hedges, one of which, возможно, turns the request into a question about whether it is possible, and the infinitive at the end has lost its subject. The reader has to work out that a deferral is wanted and that the writer is the one who wants it. One hedge is politeness; two is hesitation; three is a sentence that asks for nothing in particular.
lessons.question: Rewrite «В целях повышения эффективности работы отдела необходимо осуществление проверки исполнения обязательств» for a spoken briefing.
lessons.answer: «Чтобы отдел работал лучше, нужно проверить, как выполняются обязательства.» Each verbal noun has become a verb with a subject, and the chain of genitives has become two clauses.
lessons.distractor: «В целях повышения эффективности работы отдела нужна проверка исполнения обязательств», because replacing необходимо with нужно makes the sentence simpler.
lessons.correction: Swapping необходимо for нужно changes one word and leaves four verbal nouns in place, so the sentence is still a chain with no actor and no tense; that is lexical substitution, not unpacking. The operation has to be grammatical. Повышение эффективности comes from повысить эффективность, whose subject is the department, so it becomes «отдел работал лучше» with чтобы carrying the purpose. Осуществление проверки comes from осуществить проверку, which is itself the official periphrasis of проверить, so the whole phrase collapses to one verb, проверить. Исполнение обязательств comes from исполнять обязательства, and because the actor is unknown or unimportant it becomes the passive «как выполняются обязательства». The result has two clauses, two verbs, one purpose marker and no genitive chain, which is what a listener can follow at speaking speed. The general rule: count the nouns in -ние, -тие, -ция; each one is a verb waiting to be restored, and a sentence with three of them in a row is a sentence that has not yet been written.

depth.definitions: Вежливость (vyezh-LEE-vast) is politeness as a system of choices rather than a list of words, and косвенность (kas-VYEN-nast), 'indirectness', is the property that makes a request refusable. A номинализация (na-mee-na-lee-ZA-tsee-ya) is the conversion of a verb or adjective into a noun, and an отглагольное существительное (at-gla-GOL-na-ye soosh-CHEEST-vee-tyel-na-ye), 'deverbal noun', is the Russian term for the result: проверка from проверить, исполнение from исполнить. Канцелярит (kan-tsee-la-REET) is the name for bureaucratic style when it spreads beyond documents and deforms ordinary prose; the term was coined by Korney Chukovsky in «Живой как жизнь» (1962), as the Russian Wikipedia article records, and the campaign against it was continued by Nora Gal in «Слово живое и мёртвое» (1972). A расщеплённое сказуемое (rash-cheep-LYON-na-ye ska-ZOO-ye-ma-ye), 'split predicate', is the verb plus noun periphrasis, осуществить проверку for проверить, and it is the smallest unit of official style. Prerequisites: the compression of clause into noun in lesson 85, the summary technique of lesson 96, the unreal бы of lesson 104, the imperative politeness of lesson 69, and the suffixes -ние and -ость of lesson 107.
depth.mechanism: Both halves of this lesson are about distance, one created by grammar and one by vocabulary. «Не могли бы вы» creates distance with two markers at once: the past tense of мочь, which puts the ability in the past and therefore out of the present negotiation, and the particle бы, which marks the whole thing as unreal. A request framed as an unreal condition is one the addressee can decline without contradicting anything, and that is the linguistic content of politeness. Nominalisation creates distance of a different kind: a noun has no subject and no tense, so a sentence built from nouns cannot say who did what or when. That is a defect when the reader needs to know, and a resource when the writer needs not to say. The two mechanisms meet in the register ladder, because the bureaucratic rung uses nominalisation to avoid naming the person who failed, while the plain rung uses a first-person verb to name them. Moving down the ladder therefore restores information as well as shortening sentences, which is why a plain version is usually longer in words and shorter in reading time.
depth.secondExample: A second paragraph, this time from a report, and its plain version. Bureaucratic: «В ходе проведения проверки было установлено, что имеет место несоблюдение сроков предоставления отчётности со стороны сотрудников отдела.» (f KHO-dye pra-ve-DYE-nee-ya pra-VYER-kee BY-la oo-sta-NOV-lee-na, shto ee-MYE-yet MYE-sta nee-sab-lyoo-DYE-nee-ye SRO-kaf pre-das-tav-LYE-nee-ya at-CHOT-nas-tee sa sta-ra-NY so-trood-NEE-kaf at-DYE-la), 'in the course of the conduct of the check it was established that there takes place a failure to observe the deadlines for the submission of reporting on the part of the employees of the department'. Plain: «Проверка показала, что сотрудники отдела сдают отчёты с опозданием.» (pra-VYER-ka pa-ka-ZA-la, shto so-trood-NEE-kee at-DYE-la SDAA-yoot at-CHO-ty s ap-az-DA-nee-em), 'the check showed that the department's employees submit reports late.' The transformation is regular. В ходе проведения проверки becomes the subject проверка plus the verb показала, because the check is what did the showing. Было установлено becomes показала, an active verb with a named subject. Имеет место несоблюдение becomes сдают с опозданием, because имеет место is an empty predicate that adds nothing but gravity. Со стороны сотрудников becomes сотрудники, because the genitive after a verbal noun was the old subject all along, waiting to be restored to the nominative. That last step is the diagnostic: in a chain of genitives, one of the genitives is the real subject of the hidden verb.
depth.mistake: Four errors define the learner's version. The first is stacking politeness until the request disappears, which usually means combining не могли бы вы with если вас не затруднит and возможно; one hedge is enough, and the more polite the frame, the more specific the request must be. The second is using the formal frames where the relationship is ты: «Не могли бы вы передать соль» to a friend is a joke or an insult, and the correct frame there is the bare imperative with пожалуйста. The third is unpacking by synonym: replacing необходимо with нужно, or осуществлять with делать, leaves the nominalisation intact and produces a sentence that is still unreadable but now also ugly. The fourth is the opposite overcorrection, stripping every verbal noun out of a заявление or a regulation, where nominalisation is the correct register and the document would become unprofessional without it. Diagnostic for all four: count the hedges, count the verbal nouns, and ask who the actor is; the target is one hedge, at most two verbal nouns per sentence, and an actor you can name.
depth.application: Take one paragraph of real official Russian, a regulation, a contract clause or a university rule, of about sixty words. Count its verbal nouns and underline every genitive that follows one. Then write the paragraph three times: once as it stands, once at the neutral rung with each verbal noun restored to a verb and an actor named, and once at the plain rung as you would say it to a colleague. Read all three aloud and time them. The plain version will usually be the shortest to read and the longest to write, which is the point. Finally, take one of your own requests, a request for an extension, a reference or a meeting, and write it at the three rungs, then decide which rung the recipient's position requires. Keep the three versions in one file: they are the same content, and the ability to move between them is the skill this unit is testing.
depth.summary: A request in Russian is placed on a scale by its frame. «Не могли бы вы» with the infinitive is the most refusable and therefore the politest; «можно» plus the accusative is the everyday frame; «будьте добры» with an imperative is institutional; «разрешите» asks permission; «прошу» belongs to a document. Official style replaces verbs with nouns, and each noun hides its subject and its tense, which is useful when the writer does not want to name them and damaging when the reader needs to know. Unpacking is mechanical: restore the verb, promote one genitive to subject, and repeat until there are no chains left. The ladder from bureaucratic to plain is therefore not a matter of taste; it is a decision about how much information the reader is allowed.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Nominalization'
readings.note: Read the lead and the sections on syntactic and lexical nominalisation, which distinguish a derived noun such as проверка from a noun that simply names an action. The distinction matters for unpacking, because only the derived ones can be turned back into a verb with confidence. The article also notes that nominalisation increases information density and decreases readability, which is the trade this lesson teaches you to manage. Caveat: the article is cross-linguistic and draws most of its examples from English, so treat the Russian cases here as the application and the article as the general frame.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Deverbal nouns vs. past passive participles'
readings.note: Read the whole page, which is one screen. It gives the three formal tests that separate a deverbal noun from a past passive participle: the endings differ because the nouns are neuter, the noun stem ends in -и- after -т- or -н-, and the noun suffix has a single н while the participle has double нн. Those tests are what let you see that предложение is a noun and предложенный is a participle, which is the first step of unpacking any official sentence. Caveat: the Cyrillic is in a legacy font and decodes badly, so read the English tests and apply them to words you look up yourself.

readings.title: Википедия, «Канцелярит»
readings.note: Read the section Характеристики. The article defines канцелярит as bureaucratic style spreading beyond documents and deforming ordinary speech, records that Chukovsky coined the term in «Живой как жизнь» in 1962 on the model of the names of diseases, and notes Nora Gal's «Слово живое и мёртвое» as the continuation of the campaign. That history is why the word carries a judgement and not only a description. Caveat: the article is short, its examples are few, and the tone is polemical, so use it for the term and its provenance rather than as a style manual.

readings.title: Cornell, Beginning Russian Grammar: 'Polite imperatives'
readings.note: Read the page for the aspect contrast that underlies the imperative frames here: the imperfective imperative invites the addressee to begin and sounds friendly, while the perfective tells them to finish and sounds like an instruction. That is why «Будьте добры, продиктуйте» is acceptable in an institution, where the action is small and routine, and why the same perfective in a favour sounds like an order. Caveat: it is a 1980s textbook page with unreadable Cyrillic, so take the English explanation and supply your own examples.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Register (sociolinguistics)'
readings.note: Read the lead and the section on register as a functional variety, which gives the terminology for what this lesson calls rungs: the same content, different selections of grammar and lexis, chosen by situation rather than by speaker. The notion of a register continuum is what justifies treating bureaucratic and plain Russian as two ends of one scale rather than as two languages. Caveat: the article is general linguistics with English examples, and it says nothing about Russian official style, so pair it with the Russian sources above.

visual.title: Register ladder with a transformation column for each rung
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: three horizontal rungs labelled bureaucratic, neutral and plain, the same request written on each, and a column on the right listing the transformations that move the sentence down one rung, with the verbal nouns circled.
steps: Step 1, draw three rungs, top to bottom: bureaucratic, neutral, plain. Write the bureaucratic sentence on the top rung: В связи с отсутствием возможности осуществления оплаты в установленный договором срок прошу рассмотреть вопрос о предоставлении отсрочки.
Step 2, circle every verbal noun on the top rung and count them: отсутствие, возможность, осуществление, оплата, предоставление. Write the count in the margin. Five nouns is the diagnosis.

Step 3, fill the transformation column for the move to the neutral rung. Four entries: restore the actor as я; turn осуществление оплаты into оплатить; turn предоставление отсрочки into предоставить отсрочку; keep the contract reference but make it a relative clause with который.

Step 4, write the neutral sentence on the middle rung: Я не смог оплатить счёт в срок, указанный в договоре. Прошу предоставить отсрочку. Count the verbal nouns again and write one, отсрочка, because a document still needs its technical terms.

Step 5, fill the transformation column for the move to the plain rung. Three entries: replace прошу предоставить with можно; replace в срок, указанный в договоре with a spoken phrase; add a quantity, на неделю, because a spoken request wants a number.

Step 6, write the plain sentence on the bottom rung and read all three aloud in order. The reading time should fall as you descend while the word count stays roughly the same, and that gap is the measure of how much work the nouns were doing.

questions.prompt: A Russian office returns your application and points at the header. Which header follows the convention of a заявление?
questions.answer: «Декану исторического факультета Петрову И. И. от студента второго курса Иванова И. И.»
questions.distractor: «Декан исторического факультета Петров И. И. Студент второго курса Иванов И. И.»
questions.correction: The addressee stands in the dative and the applicant in the genitive, which is why Петрову and Иванова carry those endings; the nominative version is the inside address of an English letter, and a Russian clerk cannot tell from it that the paper is addressed to anybody. The applicant block may also be the bare genitive студента второго курса without от, which university templates use, but it may never be nominative.

questions.prompt: You are writing to a supplier who delivered two weeks late and damaged the packaging. Which pair of sentences belongs in a претензия?
questions.answer: «Прошу в течение десяти дней вернуть уплаченную сумму. В случае неисполнения я буду вынуждена обратиться в суд.»
questions.distractor: «Я очень недоволен и требую немедленно всё исправить, иначе буду жаловаться.»
questions.correction: A claim carries a specific demand with a period and a consequence that a court could act on. The second version states a feeling, gives no period that can be measured, uses требовать before any right is established, and threatens a complaint to a third party, which belongs to a жалоба and not to a претензия. The first version also needs the facts and the legal basis, but its demand and consequence are already in the right shape.

questions.prompt: You are writing for the first time to an official in a ministry whose name you know but whom you have never met. Which opening and closing pair fits?
questions.answer: «Уважаемая Ирина Викторовна! ... С уважением, Мария Соколова, группа 2-14, телефон +7 900 000 00 00.»
questions.distractor: «Добрый день! ... До свидания! Маша»
questions.correction: The first contact with an institution takes the full address with name and patronymic and the standard closing with a signature block that identifies the sender. До свидания is a spoken farewell and never closes a letter, and a bare Маша claims the intimacy of ты with somebody who has never met you. Добрый день is acceptable as a greeting, but it does not repair a closing that belongs to a different relationship.

questions.prompt: You telephone a company and a switchboard answers. Which opening does the job in Russian?
questions.answer: «Здравствуйте, вас беспокоит Иван Петров, компания «Север». Можно Сергея Петровича?»
questions.distractor: «Алло, я Иван. Мне нужно Сергей Петрович.»
questions.correction: Russian telephone identification uses это plus a name or вас беспокоит plus a surname and organisation, because the listener cannot see you and needs something to search for. «Я Иван» is a calque, a bare first name gives the switchboard nothing, and «мне нужно Сергей Петрович» states the caller's business instead of asking to be connected. The request frame is можно plus the accusative, or соедините с plus the instrumental.

questions.prompt: On the telephone you have to ask a colleague to check whether obligations are being met. Which sentence is both a real request and plain enough to say aloud?
questions.answer: «Не могли бы вы проверить, как выполняются обязательства, и сообщить до пятницы?»
questions.distractor: «В целях осуществления проверки исполнения обязательств прошу рассмотреть вопрос.»
questions.correction: The first sentence unpacks the nominalisations into two verbs, names the actor as вы, adds a deadline and uses one polite hedge, which is what a spoken request needs. The second keeps three verbal nouns, names no actor, gives no deadline and uses прошу, which belongs to a document; said aloud it asks for a review of a question rather than for a check. Swapping прошу for a warmer word would not repair it, because the problem is the noun chain.

units.title: Collocation, idiom and false friends: the verb a noun insists on, the preposition that fixes the case, work, money, weather and health, and the words that betray you

lessons.title: Collocations: the verb a noun insists on, and the four families that make them learnable
lessons.explanation:
A коллокация (ka-la-KA-tsee-ya), 'collocation', is a habitual pairing of words whose meaning is predictable from the parts but whose shape is not: Russian says принять решение (pree-NYAT ree-SHYE-nee-ye), literally 'to accept a decision', where English says make a decision and Spanish says tomar una decisión. Nothing in the meaning of принять predicts that it is the verb for decisions, and nothing in the meaning of решение predicts that it wants принять. The noun selects its verb, and the pair has to be learned as one item, in the same way as a gender or an irregular plural.

The pairs that matter most in working Russian fall into four families, and the families are what make the list learnable. The first family is decision and opinion: принять решение, 'to take a decision'; принять меры (pree-NYAT MYE-ry), 'to take measures'; вынести решение (VY-nes-tee ree-SHYE-nee-ye), 'to hand down a decision', which is what a court or a commission does; поставить вопрос (pa-STA-veet vap-ROS), 'to raise a question'; поставить под сомнение (pa-STA-veet pat sam-NYE-nee-ye), 'to call into question'; и поставить задачу (pa-STA-veet za-DA-choo), 'to set a task'. The second family is support and influence, and its light verb is оказать (a-KA-zat), 'to render': оказать помощь, 'to render assistance'; оказать поддержку, 'to give support'; оказать содействие, 'to provide cooperation'; оказать влияние на plus the accusative (a-KA-zat vlee-YA-nee-ye na), 'to exert influence on'; оказать давление на (a-KA-zat dav-LYE-nee-ye na), 'to put pressure on'. The same verb also appears in the periphrasis оказать услугу (a-KA-zat oo-SLOO-goo), 'to do a service', which is the polite way of saying that somebody helped.

The third family is conduct and performance, and its verb is провести (pra-vees-TEE), 'to conduct, to carry out': провести совещание, 'to hold a meeting'; провести исследование, 'to conduct research'; провести проверку, 'to carry out an inspection'; провести анализ, 'to carry out an analysis'; провести переговоры (pra-vees-TEE pee-ree-ga-VO-ry), 'to hold negotiations'. The fourth family is obligation and compliance: нести ответственность за plus the accusative (nees-TEE at-VYET-stven-nast za), 'to bear responsibility for'; взять на себя обязательства (vzyat na see-BYA a-bya-ZA-tyel-stva), 'to take on obligations'; соблюдать сроки (sab-lyoo-DAT SRO-kee), 'to meet deadlines'; соблюдать правила, 'to observe the rules'; выполнить обязательства (VY-pal-neet a-bya-ZA-tyel-stva), 'to fulfil obligations'; устранить недостатки (oo-stra-NEET nee-das-TAT-kee), 'to remedy defects'; и предъявить претензию (preed-ya-VEET pree-TEN-zee-yu), 'to file a claim', which is the phrase that opens the letter of lesson 122.

Two more pairs sit outside the families and cause disproportionate trouble. Играть роль (eeg-RAT rol), 'to play a role', pairs играть with роль, and иметь значение (ee-MYET zna-CHE-nee-ye), 'to matter', pairs иметь with значение; learners blend them into играть значение, which is a sentence no Russian writes. And обратить внимание на plus the accusative (ab-ra-TEET vnee-MA-nee-ye na), 'to draw attention to', is a triple fixed unit: the verb обратить, the noun внимание and the preposition на with the accusative, so «обратить внимание на проблему» is right and «обратить внимание проблеме» is not.
lessons.example:
A paragraph from a meeting protocol, with the collocations doing the work. «На совещании 14 мая мы приняли решение провести проверку сроков поставки. Отдел продаж взял на себя обязательства подготовить отчёт к 20 мая. Мы также обратили внимание на то, что поставщик не соблюдает сроки, и поставили вопрос о предъявлении претензии. Юридический отдел несёт ответственность за подготовку письма.» (na sa-vee-SHCHA-nee-ee chye-TYR-na-tsa-ta-va MA-ya my pree-NYEE-lee ree-SHYE-nee-ye pra-vees-TEE pra-VYER-koo SRO-kaf pas-TAF-kee, at-DYEL pra-DAZH vzyal na see-BYA a-bya-ZA-tyel-stva pat-ga-TO-veet at-CHOT k dvee-tsa-ta-moo MA-ya, my TAK-zhe ab-ra-TEE-lee vnee-MA-nee-ye na to, shto pas-TAF-shcheek ne sab-lyoo-DA-yet SRO-kee, ee pa-STA-vee-lee vap-ROS a preed-yav-LYE-nee-ee pree-TEN-zee-ee, yoo-ree-DEE-ches-keey at-DYEL nee-SYOT at-VYET-stven-nast za pat-ga-TOF-koo pees-MA), 'at the meeting of 14 May we decided to carry out a check of delivery deadlines. The sales department undertook to prepare a report by 20 May. We also noted that the supplier is not meeting deadlines, and raised the question of filing a claim. The legal department is responsible for preparing the letter.' Eight collocations in four sentences, and the paragraph reads as a protocol rather than as prose, which is what it is.

Now watch the aspect switch, because it is the part learners forget once they have memorised the pair. Принять is perfective, so приняли решение reports one decision taken at one meeting. The repeated or ongoing version is принимать решение (pree-nee-MAT ree-SHYE-nee-ye): «Мы принимаем такие решения каждый квартал» (my pree-nee-MA-yem ta-KEE-ye ree-SHYE-nee-ya KAZH-dy kvart-AL), 'we take such decisions every quarter'. The same switch runs through the families: оказать and оказывать, провести and проводить, заключить and заключать, достичь and достигать. The noun does not change; only the verb does, which is why the pair has to be memorised with both aspects, the way lesson 56 treated aspect pairs as a property of the verb rather than of the sentence.

Here is the learner's paragraph, with three calques. «Мы сделали решение провести контроль сроков. Отдел продаж взял обязательства сделать отчёт. Мы обратили внимание проблеме поставщика и поставили сомнение в его работе.» (my SDYE-la-lee ree-SHYE-nee-ye pra-vees-TEE kan-TROL SRO-kaf, at-DYEL pra-DAZH vzyal a-bya-ZA-tyel-stva SDYE-lat at-CHOT, my ab-ra-TEE-lee vnee-MA-nee-ye prab-LYE-mye pas-TAF-shchee-ka ee pa-STA-vee-lee sam-NYE-nee-ye v ee-VO ra-BO-tye), 'we made a decision to conduct a control of the deadlines. The sales department took obligations to make a report. We drew attention to the supplier's problem and put doubt in his work.' Every word is Russian, and three units are impossible: сделать решение, взять обязательства without на себя, and поставить сомнение, which should be поставить под сомнение with the preposition под and the accusative. The paragraph is understandable, which is exactly why the error survives: no Russian will fail to understand it, and every Russian will know within one sentence that the writer is not one.
lessons.question: A colleague drafts «Мы сделали решение провести контроль и обратили внимание проблеме поставщика». Which units are wrong, what replaces them, and why does the meaning survive?
lessons.answer: Сделали решение becomes приняли решение, провести контроль becomes провести проверку, and обратили внимание проблеме becomes обратили внимание на проблему; the meaning survives because each wrong verb is a near synonym of the right one, so the reader reconstructs the intended pair.
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong; Russian official style allows synonymous verbs, and сделать is the neutral verb for any action.
lessons.correction: Three units fail and each fails in a different way. Сделать решение is a calque of make a decision, and the Russian verb for decisions is принять, which is why the phrase sounds translated rather than wrong. Провести контроль is a near miss: Russian does say контроль, but the collocation with провести is провести проверку, while контроль is what you have or establish, as in установить контроль. Обратить внимание requires на plus the accusative, because the phrase is a triple unit and the preposition is part of it, so the bare dative проблеме has no support. The meaning survives because collocations are redundant: the noun решение already carries enough meaning for the reader to supply принять, and the same is true of внимание and на. That redundancy is why these errors do not block communication and why they are so persistent, since nothing in the situation ever forces the learner to notice them. The repair is to memorise the noun with its verb and its preposition as one string, not to learn the verb separately and hope it fits.

depth.definitions: A коллокация is a habitual word pairing whose parts keep their meaning, as against a фразеологизм (fra-zee-a-LO-geezm), 'idiom', whose meaning cannot be computed from the parts: принять решение is a collocation, while бить баклуши, 'to idle', is an idiom, which lesson 128 treats. A расщеплённое сказуемое is the verb plus noun periphrasis that official style prefers, оказать помощь for помочь, and lesson 125 showed how to unpack it. A лёгкий глагол (LYOKH-keey gla-GOL), 'light verb', is a verb that contributes aspect, tense and person but little lexical meaning, and принять, оказать, провести, нести and дать are the five that carry most of working Russian. Управление (oop-rav-LYE-nee-ye), 'government', is the case a verb or noun requires of its dependent, and collocations must be learned together with their government: обратить внимание на plus accusative, нести ответственность за plus accusative, принимать участие в plus prepositional. Prerequisites: the aspect pairs of lesson 56, the split predicates and register ladder of lesson 125, and the noun suffixes of lesson 107, which predict that a noun in -ние will usually want a light verb rather than a full one.
depth.mechanism: Collocations exist because languages divide the labour between a verb and its object differently, and Russian gives the noun most of the lexical content while the verb carries the grammar. Принять contributes aspect, tense and agreement and almost nothing else; решение contributes the meaning. That division is productive in one direction and arbitrary in the other: the same light verb can take a whole family of nouns, which is why оказать помощь, поддержку, содействие, влияние and давление can be learned as a set, but the choice of light verb for a given noun is a lexical fact that no rule generates. The mechanism also explains why the aspect switch is regular while the verb choice is not. Once you know that the pair is принять решение, the imperfective is automatically принимать решение, because aspect is a property of the verb paradigm; but knowing that решение takes принять tells you nothing about whether вывод takes сделать or прийти к, which is why the pairs are learned noun by noun. The families are the compromise: they do not predict, but they organise, and an organised list of forty pairs is learnable in a way that a random list of forty is not.
depth.secondExample: An email that uses six collocations in eight lines, with the aspect choices visible. «Уважаемая Ирина Викторовна! По итогам совещания 14 мая мы приняли решение провести проверку соблюдения сроков. Прошу вас оказать содействие в подготовке отчёта: отдел продаж несёт ответственность за цифры, юридический отдел за формулировки. Если поставщик не устранит недостатки до 20 мая, мы предъявим претензию. Заключение договора на новый срок возможно только после устранения нарушений. С уважением, М. С. Петрова.» (pa EE-to-gam sa-vee-SHCHA-nee-ya chye-TYR-na-tsa-ta-va MA-ya my pree-NYEE-lee ree-SHYE-nee-ye pra-vees-TEE pra-VYER-koo sab-lyoo-DYE-nee-ya SRO-kaf, pra-SHOO vas a-KA-zat sa-DYEYS-tvee-ye f pat-ga-TOF-kye at-CHO-ta, at-DYEL pra-DAZH nee-SYOT at-VYET-stven-nast za TSEE-fry, yoo-ree-DEE-ches-keey at-DYEL za far-moo-LEEF-kee, YES-lee pas-TAF-shcheek ne oos-tra-NEET nee-das-TAT-kee da dvee-tsa-ta-va MA-ya, my preed-YA-veem pree-TEN-zee-yu, za-klyoo-CHE-nee-ye da-ga-VO-ra na NO-vy SROK vaz-MOZH-na TOL-ka POS-lye oos-tra-NYE-nee-ya na-roo-SHYE-nee-y), 'Dear Irina Viktorovna, following the meeting of 14 May we decided to carry out a check of compliance with deadlines. I ask you to assist in preparing the report: the sales department is responsible for the figures, the legal department for the wording. If the supplier does not remedy the defects by 20 May, we will file a claim. Concluding a contract for a new term is possible only after the breaches are remedied.' Note four things. Приняли is perfective because the decision was taken once, while предъявим is future perfective because the claim is one future act, and возможно is the short adjective that carries the modal meaning without a verb. Несёт ответственность за takes the accusative of the thing, and the second half of the sentence repeats за with a second accusative, which is normal in this construction. And заключение договора is the nominalisation of заключить договор, so the same collocation appears twice in the letter in two grammatical forms, once as a verb phrase and once as a noun phrase, which is exactly the register ladder of lesson 125 applied to a single pair.
depth.mistake: Four errors dominate. The first is translating the English light verb: сделать решение, сделать вывод is correct but сделать решение is not, and take measures becomes принять меры, not взять меры. The second is blending two pairs that share a noun, as in играть значение, which mixes играть роль and иметь значение; the same blend produces одержать победу, 'to win', used with a noun that does not collocate, and оказать решение, which mixes the support family with the decision family. The third is dropping the preposition that belongs to the pair: обратить внимание проблеме, нести ответственность, поставить сомнение, all of which are missing a на, за or под that the collocation requires. The fourth is aspect: using the perfective for a repeated action, as in «мы приняли такие решения каждый квартал», where the adverb каждый forces the imperfective принимали. Diagnostic for all four: store each collocation as a string with its preposition and both aspects, verb plus noun plus government, and test a new sentence by asking what the noun is, not what the verb should be.
depth.application: Build a twelve-row collocation grid from one source, a contract, a regulation, a news report or the protocol above. Columns: the noun, the light verb, the aspect pair, the government, and one sentence of your own. Fill it only with pairs you have seen in the source, not with pairs you have translated. Then write a one-paragraph protocol about a real or invented meeting using at least eight of the twelve, and check each row against the grid. Next, take the same paragraph and move it one rung down the lesson 125 ladder, replacing three light verb phrases with single verbs: провести проверку becomes проверить, оказать содействие becomes помочь, принять решение becomes решить. Notice which replacements sound natural in a protocol and which do not, and keep the ones that do not, because a protocol is a genre where the periphrasis is correct. Thirty minutes, and the grid is reusable for the rest of the course.
depth.summary: A collocation is a habitual pair whose meaning is transparent and whose shape is arbitrary, and in Russian the noun chooses the verb. Learn the pairs in families: принять for decisions and measures, оказать for assistance and influence, провести for meetings, research and inspections, нести and взять на себя for obligation, поставить for questions and doubts. Learn the government with the pair, на plus accusative for внимание, за plus accusative for ответственность, под plus accusative for сомнение. Learn both aspects of the verb, because the noun never changes and the aspect always does. The errors do not block understanding, which is precisely why they need deliberate practice.

readings.title: Википедия, «Коллокация»
readings.note: Read the lead and the section on types of collocation, which distinguishes free combinations, collocations and idioms by how fixed the pairing is. That scale is the frame for this lesson: принять решение is fixed enough to be a unit, while красная машина is free. Caveat: the article is short, it is written from a general and partly corpus-linguistic point of view, and its examples are not Russian, so use it for the concept and take the Russian pairs from the item list.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'Collocation'
readings.note: Read the lead and the section on collocation in corpus linguistics, which explains the statistical notion of words that occur together more often than chance would predict. That notion is why a collocation can be transparent and still obligatory: frequency, not logic, fixes the pair. Caveat: the article is about English and about corpus method, and it offers no Russian data, so read it for the definition and the mechanism.

readings.title: Викисловарь, «принять»
readings.note: Read the Значение section, where the senses are listed in order and the decision sense appears among them, and note the stress on the second syllable, приня́ть. Seeing that принять has a dozen senses, from accepting a parcel to taking a decision to taking medicine, is the argument for learning the pair rather than the verb: the noun is what tells you which sense is active. Caveat: a dictionary lists senses but does not mark which combinations are fixed, so it cannot tell you that принять решение is a unit while принять совет is not.

readings.title: Викисловарь, «оказать»
readings.note: Read the Значение section and the examples. The verb is defined as showing or providing something, and its examples are exactly the support family: помощь, содействие, услуга, внимание. That is the clearest single demonstration that a light verb comes with a set of nouns rather than with a meaning you can generalise. Caveat: the entry is compact and does not list the whole family, and its examples are not glossed, so check any new pair in a dictionary entry for the noun before using it.

readings.title: Викисловарь, «провести»
readings.note: Read the Значение section. The senses run from leading somebody somewhere to spending time to carrying out an activity, and the last is the one that builds совещание, исследование, проверку and анализ. The entry is also where you can check the aspect pair, провести and проводить, which is the switch that repeats through the whole family. Caveat: dictionaries record senses, not collocational preferences, so the entry will not tell you that провести контроль is weaker than провести проверку.

visual.title: Light-verb grid: five verbs by four noun families
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: a grid with five light verbs down the left column, принять, оказать, провести, нести, поставить, and four noun families across the top, decisions, support, conduct, obligation. Each cell holds a model collocation or is marked empty, and a footnote records the government.
steps: Step 1, draw the grid: five rows for принять, оказать, провести, нести, поставить, and four columns for решения, поддержка, проведение, обязательства. Keep the cells small, one phrase each.

Step 2, fill the diagonal and note how full it is. Принять plus решение, оказать plus помощь, провести plus совещание, нести plus ответственность, поставить plus вопрос. The grid is mostly empty, which is the visual proof that the pair is lexical and not generated.

Step 3, fill the support row across the columns. Оказать takes помощь, поддержку, содействие, влияние and давление, so that row is full; write all five in the cell and mark it as a family, the one place where the grid does predict.

Step 4, add the government column. Under each collocation write the case it requires: на plus accusative for обратить внимание, за plus accusative for нести ответственность, под plus accusative for поставить под сомнение, в plus prepositional for принимать участие. Government is part of the item, not an add-on.

Step 5, add a second row under each verb for the imperfective. Принимать, оказывать, проводить, нести, ставить. Bracket the two rows and write aspect pair beside them, because the noun never changes and the verb always alternates.

Step 6, test a new sentence. Take a sentence you have written and place each verb in the grid. If the cell is empty, you have either invented a pair or translated one; look up the noun and rewrite the verb before the sentence goes out.

lessons.title: The preposition decides the case: the fixed phrases of official Russian and the four that break the pattern
lessons.explanation:
Official Russian is held together by prepositional phrases, and every one of them carries a case that the writer has to supply. Three groups cover almost everything. The first group is built on с and takes the instrumental: «в соответствии с договором» (v sa-at-VYET-stvee s da-ga-VO-rom), 'in accordance with the contract'; «в связи с изменением сроков» (v SVYA-zee s eez-mee-NYE-nee-em SRO-kaf), 'in connection with the change of deadlines'; «наряду с другими мерами» (na-rya-DOO s droo-GEE-mee MYE-ra-mee), 'along with other measures'. The second group takes the genitive, and it is the largest, because the genitive has become the default case for new prepositions: «в течение месяца» (f tee-CHE-nee-ye MYE-sya-tsa), 'within a month'; «в целях экономии» (f TSE-lyakh e-ka-no-MEE-ee), 'for the purpose of saving'; «на основании статьи 128» (na as-na-VA-nee-ee stat-EE STO DVA-tsat va-see-MO-va), 'on the basis of article 128'; «в отношении сотрудника» (v at-na-SHYE-nee-ee so-trood-NEE-ka), 'with regard to the employee'; «за счёт средств фонда» (za SHCHOT SRYET-staf FON-da), 'at the expense of the fund'; «в случае отказа» (f SLOO-cha-ye at-KA-za), 'in the event of refusal'; «во избежание ошибок» (va eez-bye-ZHA-nee-ye a-SHEE-bak), 'in order to avoid mistakes'; «по истечении срока» (pa ees-tee-CHE-nee-ee SRO-ka), 'upon expiry of the period'; и «вследствие нарушения обязательств» (FSLYET-stvee-ye na-roo-SHYE-nee-ya a-bya-ZA-tyel-stv), 'as a consequence of the breach of obligations'.

The third group takes the dative, and it is the group that costs learners the most marks. «Согласно договору» (sag-LAS-na da-ga-VO-roo), 'according to the contract'; «благодаря поддержке» (bla-ga-da-RYA pat-DYERZH-kye), 'thanks to the support'; «вопреки ожиданиям» (vap-ree-KEE a-zhee-DA-nee-yam), 'contrary to expectations'; «наперекор традиции» (na-pee-ree-KOR tra-DEE-tsee-ee), 'in defiance of tradition'. The list is closed and short, and the reason it behaves this way is visible in the words themselves. Согласно, вопреки and наперекор are former adverbs, and благодаря is a former gerund of благодарить, so none of them began life as a preposition; as the alphaDictionary page on dative prepositions puts it, the forms often thought to be dative prepositions are in fact participles and adverbs, and that is why they do not follow the genitive default. Functionally the dative is the case of the recipient and the beneficiary, which fits the meanings: these phrases all name a party toward whom the action is oriented, whether as a source of authority, a source of help, or a point of resistance.

Four minimal pairs decide whether the sentence is literate, and they are all about the difference between a preposition and a noun that looks like one. «В течение недели» (f tee-CHE-nee-ye nee-DYE-lee) is 'within a week' and ends in -ее; «в течении реки» (f tee-CHE-nee-ee ree-KEE) is 'in the current of the river' and ends in -ии, because it is the prepositional case of the noun течение. «Вследствие ошибки» (FSLYET-stvee-ye a-SHEEP-kee) means 'as a consequence of an error' and is written as one word; «в следствие» with a space would be 'into the investigation', which is a different phrase and needs a context like передать материалы в следствие. «По истечении срока» takes the genitive because the phrase means 'after the period has expired', while «по договору» takes the dative because по there means 'according to'; the two по are historically the same preposition and behave differently because their meanings are different. And «в соответствии с» cannot be shortened to «в соответствии» plus the dative: the с is part of the phrase and the instrumental is its consequence.
lessons.example:
A paragraph from a rule sheet, with every phrase parsed. «В соответствии с пунктом 5 договора оплата производится в течение десяти банковских дней с момента подписания акта. Согласно приложению 2 сроки могут быть продлены по истечении указанного периода. В случае нарушения сроков исполнитель уплачивает неустойку в размере 0,1 процента за каждый день просрочки. В целях урегулирования спора стороны проводят переговоры. В отношении требований, не урегулированных договором, применяются нормы Гражданского кодекса.» (v sa-at-VYET-stvee s POONK-tam PYA-ta-va da-ga-VO-ra ap-LA-ta pra-ees-VO-deet-sya f tee-CHE-nee-ye dee-see-TEE ban-KOF-skikh dnyey s ma-MYEN-ta pat-pee-SA-nee-ya AK-ta, sag-LAS-na pree-la-ZHYE-nee-yu DVA SRO-kee MO-goot byt pra-DLYE-ny pa ees-tee-CHE-nee-ee oo-KA-zan-na-va pee-ree-O-da, f SLOO-cha-ye na-roo-SHYE-nee-ya SRO-kaf ees-pal-NEE-tyel oop-la-CHEE-va-yet nee-oos-TOY-koo v raz-MYE-rye NOOL TSEE-lykh a-DEEN pra-TSEN-ta za KAZH-dy dyen pra-SROCH-kee, f TSE-lyakh oo-ree-goo-LEE-ra-va-nee-ya SPO-ra STO-ra-ny pra-VO-dyat pee-ree-ga-VO-ry, v at-na-SHYE-nee-ee TRYE-ba-va-nee, ne oo-ree-goo-LEE-ra-van-nykh da-ga-VO-rom, pree-mee-NYA-yut-sya NOR-my Grazh-DAN-ska-va KO-dek-sa), 'in accordance with clause 5 of the contract, payment is made within ten banking days of the signing of the act. According to appendix 2 the deadlines may be extended upon expiry of the stated period. In the event of breach of deadlines the contractor pays a penalty of 0.1 per cent for each day of delay. For the purpose of settling the dispute the parties hold negotiations. With regard to claims not settled by the contract, the norms of the Civil Code apply.'

Five phrases, five cases, and each one can be checked by its ending: договором is instrumental after с, десяти банковских дней is genitive after в течение, приложению is dative after согласно, истечении is genitive after по, нарушения is genitive after в случае, урегулирования is genitive after в целях, and требований is genitive after в отношении. A reader who knows the four groups can parse the paragraph without understanding the contract, which is exactly the skill this lesson is teaching.

Now the learner's version. «Согласно договора оплата производится в течении десяти дней. В соответствие с приложением сроки продлеваются по истечение периода. Благодаря нарушения сроков исполнитель платит неустойку.» (sag-LAS-na da-ga-VO-ra ap-LA-ta pra-ees-VO-deet-sya f tee-CHE-nee-ee dee-see-TEE dnyey, v sa-at-VYET-stvee-ee s pree-la-ZHYE-nee-em SRO-kee pra-dlye-VA-yut-sya pa ees-tee-CHE-nee-ye pee-ree-O-da, bla-ga-da-RYA na-roo-SHYE-nee-ya SRO-kaf ees-pal-NEE-tyel PLA-teet nee-oos-TOY-koo), 'according to the contract payment is made in the course of ten days. In accordance with the appendix the deadlines are extended upon the expiry of the period. Thanks to the breach of deadlines the contractor pays a penalty.' Four errors. Договора should be договору after согласно. В течении should be в течение, because the preposition ends in -ее and the noun does not. В соответствие should be в соответствии, because the phrase is in the prepositional case and the -ие nouns keep -ии there. По истечение should be по истечении. And благодаря is the fifth error, a semantic one: it names a good outcome, so using it of a breach reads as irony, and the neutral formal word is вследствие or в результате.
lessons.question: A contract clause reads «Согласно договора оплата производится в течение 10 дней». Which word is wrong, and why does the wrong form feel right to a learner?
lessons.answer: Договора should be договору, because согласно governs the dative; the genitive feels right because most Russian prepositions, and almost all the long compound ones, take the genitive.
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong; согласно can take either case, and the genitive is the more formal choice in contracts.
lessons.correction: Согласно belongs to a closed set of four words, согласно, благодаря, вопреки, наперекор, which govern the dative. The feeling that договора is correct comes from a real pattern that the learner has already internalised: the genitive is the default case for prepositions in Russian, and the long official phrases in -ние, в течение, в целях, на основании, в отношении, в случае, all take it, so a learner who has read a hundred contract clauses has seen a hundred genitives and generalises. The exception is small enough to memorise and important enough to mark, because it appears in the first line of most contracts. Two supporting habits make it stick: learn the four words as a chant with a dative noun attached, согласно договору, благодаря поддержке, вопреки ожиданиям, наперекор традиции; and learn the reason, that these are former adverbs and gerunds rather than original prepositions, so they kept the government of the words they came from. The same clause also tests в течение, which is correct here because it means 'within', and the ending -ее is the mark of the preposition.

depth.definitions: A предлог (preed-LOK), 'preposition', governs the case of the noun after it, and управление is the name for that relation. A производный предлог (pra-ees-VOD-ny preed-LOK), 'derived preposition', is one formed from another part of speech: благодаря from a gerund, согласно and вопреки from adverbs, в течение from a noun phrase. A предложное сочетание (pre-LOZH-na-ye sa-chee-TA-nee-ye) is a fixed phrase that functions as a preposition, such as в соответствии с or в связи с. The three cases at stake are the genitive, the default for derived prepositions and for the compound phrases in -ние; the dative, required by the four words that name a party toward whom the action is oriented; and the instrumental, required by the phrases built on с. Two homonyms to keep apart: течение as a preposition, in the accusative form в течение, and течение as a noun, 'current', whose prepositional is в течении. Prerequisites: the genitive after prepositions in lesson 53, the dative in lesson 61, the instrumental in lesson 63, and the official formulas of lessons 122 and 125.
depth.mechanism: The case after a preposition is not chosen by the writer; it is a property of the preposition, and the property is historical. Original prepositions such as в, на, с, от, из have governed their cases for centuries and are learned early. Derived prepositions inherit the government of the word they came from, which is why the set is irregular: a phrase that began as a noun in the accusative, в течение, keeps the genitive its noun required; a word that began as an adverb, согласно, keeps the dative that adverbs of orientation took. Because the genitive has become the productive case for new prepositions, the irregular set is closed and small, and that is good news: four words cover the dative exceptions, and the rest of official Russian is genitive or instrumental. The mechanism also explains the minimal pairs. В течение and в течении are not two spellings of one thing; one is a preposition built from a noun in the accusative, the other is that noun in the prepositional, and the difference in ending is the difference between a function word and a content word. The same logic separates вследствие from в следствие and по истечении from a mistaken по истечение.
depth.secondExample: A second paragraph, this time from a letter, where the phrases carry the argument rather than the compliance. «В связи с неисполнением обязательств по договору № 14 и на основании пункта 7.2 прошу в течение десяти дней устранить недостатки. В случае неисполнения мы будем вынуждены обратиться в суд. В отношении неустойки сообщаю, что она начисляется согласно приложению 3. Благодаря своевременному вмешательству вашего инженера часть оборудования удалось восстановить, за что мы признательны.» (v SVYA-zee s ne-ees-pal-NYE-nee-em a-bya-ZA-tyel-stv pa da-ga-VO-roo chye-TYR-na-tsat ee na as-na-VA-nee-ee POONK-ta syem da dva pra-SHOO f tee-CHE-nee-ye dee-see-TEE dnyey oos-tra-NEET nee-das-TAT-kee, f SLOO-cha-ye ne-ees-pal-NYE-nee-ya my BOO-dem VY-noozh-dee-ny ab-ra-TEET-sya f soot, v at-na-SHYE-nee-ee nee-oos-TOY-kee sa-ap-SHCHA-yoo, shto a-NA na-chees-LYA-yet-sya sag-LAS-na pree-la-ZHYE-nee-yu tree, bla-ga-da-RYA svye-ef-ree-MYEN-na-moo vmye-SHA-tyel-stvo VA-she-va een-zhee-NYE-ra chast a-ba-ROO-da-va-nee-ya oo-da-LOS vas-sta-na-VEET, za shto my pree-ZNA-tyel-ny), 'in connection with the non-performance of obligations under contract 14 and on the basis of clause 7.2, I ask that the defects be remedied within ten days. In the event of non-performance we will be obliged to go to court. With regard to the penalty, I inform you that it is charged in accordance with appendix 3. Thanks to the timely intervention of your engineer, part of the equipment was recovered, for which we are grateful.' Note what the last sentence does. Благодаря is used of a good outcome and a person, which is its proper domain, and the sentence then thanks the person by name of role. A writer who had used благодаря for the breach in the previous sentence would have produced irony; here the same preposition carries genuine gratitude. That contrast is the semantic half of the lesson, and it matters as much as the case endings, because a correctly declined благодаря in the wrong sentence is still an error of register.
depth.mistake: Five errors recur. The first is согласно plus the genitive, the single most common case error in Russian business writing. The second is the spelling of в течение: learners write в течении because they hear no difference and because -ии is frequent in the prepositional case of -ие nouns; the preposition ends in -ее. The third is по истечение for по истечении, produced by the same hearing problem and by the temptation to treat по as a dative or accusative preposition. The fourth is в соответствие for в соответствии, where the phrase is in the prepositional and the noun keeps -ии. The fifth is semantic: using благодаря for a bad outcome, as in благодаря ошибке, which is either irony or a mistake, since the neutral words are из-за for a cause with a negative colour and вследствие or в результате for a formal neutral cause. Diagnostic for all five: cover the noun and look only at the preposition; if it is one of the four dative words, the ending must be -у, -е or -ам; if it ends in -ние, the noun after it is genitive; if it contains с, the noun is instrumental.
depth.application: Build a phrase bank of twenty official phrases in three columns, genitive, dative and instrumental, and put each phrase in the column of the case it governs, not the case it looks like. Add a fourth column for the minimal pairs, в течение against в течении, вследствие against в следствие, по истечении against по истечение, and write one sentence for each member of each pair. Then take a real contract or regulation of one page and underline every prepositional phrase, labelling its case in the margin. Count how many are genitive, how many instrumental and how many dative; the proportions will be roughly seventy, twenty and ten, which is the practical reason the genitive default exists. Finally, write a one-page rule sheet for a procedure you know, using at least five phrases from the bank, and read it aloud: a phrase that you cannot decline at speaking speed is one you have not yet learned.
depth.summary: The case after a preposition belongs to the preposition. Three groups cover official Russian: the phrases built on с take the instrumental, the long compound phrases in -ние and the great majority of derived prepositions take the genitive, and a closed set of four, согласно, благодаря, вопреки and наперекор, takes the dative. The dative set is irregular because those words are former adverbs and gerunds, and the genitive default exists because it is the productive case for new prepositions. Four minimal pairs, в течение against в течении, вследствие against в следствие, по истечении against по истечение, and в соответствии against в соответствие, decide whether the page looks literate. And благодаря carries a positive evaluation, so a correct ending in the wrong sentence is still wrong.

steps: Step 1, draw three columns and head them genitive, dative, instrumental. Write the question each case answers above the column: genitive, of what; dative, to what; instrumental, with what.

Step 2, fill the genitive column with six phrases and a model ending: в течение месяца, в целях экономии, на основании статьи, в отношении сотрудника, в случае отказа, по истечении срока. Underline the -а, -и, -я endings and note that every one is genitive singular.

Step 3, fill the dative column with the four irregular words and a model: согласно договору, благодаря поддержке, вопреки ожиданиям, наперекор традиции. Draw a box around the column and label it closed set, four words, dative only.

Step 4, fill the instrumental column with the с phrases: в соответствии с договором, в связи с изменением, наряду с другими мерами. Underline the -ом, -ем, -ами endings and connect the с to the column heading with an arrow.

Step 5, draw the minimal-pair strip under the table, four pairs on one line each: в течение against в течении, вследствие against в следствие, по истечении against по истечение, в соответствии against в соответствие. Beside each pair write one word naming the difference: preposition against noun, one word against two, genitive against a mistake, prepositional against the wrong case.

Step 6, test a sentence. Take a clause from a contract and place each phrase in a column. A phrase that fits no column is either a simple preposition you already know or an error, and the two can be told apart by checking the noun's ending against the column.

lessons.title: Idioms of work and money: what each one promises, and the contexts that forbid it
lessons.explanation:
A фразеологизм (fra-zee-a-LO-geezm), 'idiom', is a fixed expression whose meaning cannot be computed from its parts. Бить баклуши (beet bak-LOO-shee) has nothing to do with beating anything; it means 'to idle', and the word баклуши survives only inside this phrase. That is the first test of an idiom and the reason it must be learned whole: the literal image is dead, and only the idiomatic meaning circulates. The second test is grammatical. Idioms resist modification: you cannot swap a synonym, add an adjective freely, or change the aspect of the verb at will, and the forms inside them are often fossils. Не покладая рук (ne pak-la-DA-ya rook), 'without a break', contains a gerund of positive imperfective meaning that occurs nowhere else in the language; lesson 72 taught gerunds as a productive tool, and this is the one place where a gerund is frozen into a phrase and cannot be rebuilt.

Work idioms divide by the stance they take. The complimentary ones praise: работать не покладая рук, 'to work without letting one's hands rest', used in praise and in obituaries, slightly bookish and never ironic; держать руку на пульсе (deer-ZHAT ROO-koo na POOL-sye), 'to keep a finger on the pulse', a business cliché that is acceptable in speech and dead on the page. The critical ones judge: бить баклуши, 'to idle', which is old-fashioned and sounds like a grandparent's reproach; тянуть резину (tee-NOOT rye-ZEE-noo), 'to drag it out', the standard complaint about a delay and the most usable idiom in this set; делать из мухи слона (DYE-lat eez MOO-khee sla-NA), 'to make a mountain out of a molehill'; и семь пятниц на неделе (syem PYAT-neets na nee-DYE-lye), 'seven Fridays in a week', said of a person who keeps changing their mind, and only of a person, never of a plan or a schedule. The self-directed ones advise: взять себя в руки (vzyat see-BYA v ROO-kee), 'to pull oneself together', which is a resolution when you say it of yourself and a rebuke when you say it to somebody else; и как белка в колесе (kak BYEL-ka v ka-lee-SYE), 'like a squirrel in a wheel', said of constant motion without progress, which Russians use about themselves far more often than about others.

Money idioms carry the same double edge. Сидеть на мели (see-DYET na mye-LEE), literally 'to sit on a shoal', means 'to be broke' and is the mildest of the set. Считать копейки (shee-TAT ka-PYEY-kee), 'to count every kopeck', describes genuine poverty or exaggerated thrift, and the context decides which. Затянуть пояс (za-tee-NOOT PO-yas), 'to tighten one's belt', is about a household or an organisation cutting spending. Жить на широкую ногу (zheet na shee-ROO-koo-yu NO-goo), 'to live in grand style', is neutral description when the subject is a stranger and envious when the subject is present. Денег куры не клюют (DYE-nek KOO-ry ne klyoo-YOOT), 'the chickens do not peck at the money', means 'rolling in money' and is the most loaded of all, because it is almost always said about somebody else with a mixture of admiration and resentment. Вылететь в трубу (VY-lee-tyet v troo-BOO), 'to fly out through the chimney', means 'to be ruined, to go broke', and it is strong: it belongs to a person or a company, not to a project, and it is the idiom most likely to be misused by a learner who likes its colour. Откладывать на чёрный день (at-KLA-dy-vat na CHOR-ny dyen), 'to put aside for a black day', is the neutral phrase for saving, and it is the only one in the money set that can appear in a conversation about personal finance without any irony.

What all of them share is a register ceiling. An idiom presupposes a shared evaluation between speaker and hearer, which is why it belongs to speech, to a message between colleagues, to a toast, or to a comment on somebody else's behaviour. In a document it does something else: it either editorialises, as не покладая рук does in a report, or it ironises, as вылететь в трубу does in a financial summary. The test is not whether the idiom is correct, because all of these are correct Russian, but whether the genre allows the speaker to have an opinion about the facts. A заявление, a претензия, a contract and a news report do not.
lessons.example:
A spoken exchange between two colleagues, then the same content in writing. «Ты почему отчёт не сдал? Опять резину тянешь?» «Не тяну я резину, у меня было три совещания. Я как белка в колесе.» «Ладно, возьми себя в руки и сдай до пятницы.» «Сдам. Но если они опять поменяют требования, я не виноват: у них семь пятниц на неделе.» (ty pa-chee-MOO at-CHOT ne zdal, a-PYAT rye-ZEE-noo TYA-nesh, ne tee-NOO ya rye-ZEE-noo, oo mee-NYA BY-la tree sa-vee-SHCHA-nee-ya, ya kak BYEL-ka v ka-lee-SYE, LA-da, vaz-MEE see-BYA v ROO-kee ee zdyey da PYAT-nee-tsy, zdam, no YES-lee a-NEE a-PYAT pa-MYE-nya-yoot TRYE-ba-va-nee-ya, ya ne vee-na-VAT, oo neekh syem PYAT-neets na nee-DYE-lye), 'why have you not submitted the report? Are you dragging it out again? I am not dragging anything out, I had three meetings. I am like a squirrel in a wheel. All right, pull yourself together and submit it by Friday. I will. But if they change the requirements again it is not my fault: with them it is seven Fridays in a week.' Four idioms, all in the second person or the first, all evaluative, and the exchange works because both speakers share the evaluation and neither is writing anything down.

The same content as a report: «Отчёт не был представлен в срок, поскольку сотрудник был занят участием в трёх совещаниях. Требования к отчёту изменялись трижды, что затруднило подготовку. Отчёт будет представлен до пятницы.» (at-CHOT ne byl preet-STA-vlyen f SROK, pa-SKOL-koo so-trood-NEET byl ZA-nyat oo-CHA-stee-em f tryokh sa-vee-SHCHA-nee-yakh, TRYE-ba-va-nee-ya k at-CHO-too eez-mee-NYA-lees tree-zhdy, shto za-trood-NEE-la pat-ga-TOF-koo, at-CHOT BOO-det preet-STA-vlyen da PYAT-nee-tsy), 'the report was not submitted on time because the employee was occupied with attending three meetings. The requirements for the report changed three times, which made preparation difficult. The report will be submitted by Friday.' Every idiom has vanished and nothing has been lost except the opinion. That is the whole difference: the report keeps the facts and the causal links, and it drops the stance, which is exactly what lesson 125's register ladder predicted.

Now the version that fails, from a learner's report: «Отдел работал не покладая рук, но проект вылетел в трубу, и все сидят на мели.» (at-DYEL ra-BO-tal ne pak-la-DA-ya rook, no pra-YEKT VY-lee-tyel v troo-BOO, ee vsye see-DYAT na mye-LEE), 'the department worked tirelessly, but the project flew out of the chimney, and everybody is sitting on a shoal.' Three idioms in one sentence, one of them complimentary and two catastrophic, produce comedy rather than a finding; the project is the wrong kind of subject for вылететь в трубу, which wants a person or a firm; and все сидят на мели is a claim about colleagues that a report has no business making.
lessons.question: In a financial report you write «Проект вылетел в трубу, поэтому отдел сидит на мели». What is wrong, and what should the sentence say?
lessons.answer: Both idioms are colloquial and evaluative, and вылететь в трубу takes a person or a company rather than a project; a report needs the neutral formulation, «проект был признан нерентабельным, поэтому расходы отдела сокращены».
lessons.distractor: Nothing is wrong with the wording; the only problem is that the report does not give the amount of the loss.
lessons.correction: Two separate faults, one of register and one of collocation. The register fault is that both idioms put the writer's attitude into a genre that reports facts: вылететь в трубу is slang for ruin and сидеть на мели is a conversational phrase for being broke, and a financial report cannot afford either, because the reader will suspect that the numbers are being replaced by adjectives. The collocation fault is that вылететь в трубу selects a human or corporate subject, the one who is ruined, not the venture that caused the ruin; a project can be закрыт, приостановлен, признан нерентабельным, but it cannot fly out of a chimney. The repaired sentence names the finding and the consequence in the passive or the neuter: «Проект признан нерентабельным, расходы отдела сокращены на двадцать процентов». If you want the human cost, state it as a fact rather than an idiom: «два сотрудника переведены на неполную ставку». The general rule from lesson 125 applies here in lexical form: an idiom is a stance, and a stance belongs in a genre that has a speaker.

depth.definitions: A фразеологизм is a fixed multi-word unit whose meaning is not the sum of its parts, and идиома is the narrower term for the ones whose literal reading is unavailable, as with бить баклуши. A клише (klee-SHE), 'cliché', is a phrase whose frequency has worn out its expressiveness, and держать руку на пульсе is one. Замороженная форма (za-ma-RO-zhen-na-ya FOR-ma), 'frozen form', is the grammatical fossil inside an idiom, such as the gerund in не покладая рук or the genitive plural баклуши, which has no singular in use. Экспрессивная лексика is vocabulary that carries evaluation, and every idiom in this lesson is expressive. Register, as lesson 125 defined it, is the selection of grammar and lexis that a situation permits, and it is the variable that decides whether an idiom is usable. Prerequisites: the gerunds of lesson 72, the stance particles of lesson 102, the register ladder of lesson 125, and the collocation principle of lesson 126, which this lesson extends from transparent pairs to opaque ones.
depth.mechanism: An idiom is stored as a single lexical entry with a fixed syntactic shape, and that is why it resists the substitutions that ordinary phrases allow. If you know the phrase as a unit, you cannot generate a variant, because the variant is not in the lexicon; a learner who says бить доски has correctly applied the rule and produced something that does not exist. The same storage explains why the register is fixed. An idiom's meaning includes an evaluation, and an evaluation presupposes a speaker who is entitled to make it; in a document, the institution is the speaker, and institutions do not have opinions about whether somebody is a squirrel in a wheel. The grammar inside the idiom also tends to be archaic, which is a useful signal: when a phrase contains a form you cannot rebuild, such as не покладая or в колесе, you are looking at a fossil and should learn it as a word. Finally, idioms cluster by domain because the images come from shared experience: work idioms come from farming, crafts and the office, money idioms from coins and households, and weather idioms from agriculture. The domain is a memory hook, not a rule of use.
depth.secondExample: A negotiation, where the idioms are doing relational work rather than describing. «Мы понимаем, что вы сидите на мели, но и мы не можем работать себе в убыток.» «Не надо делать из мухи слона. Мы не сидим на мели, просто деньги придут в конце месяца.» «Хорошо, давайте не тянуть резину: вы платите половину сейчас, половину через две недели.» «Согласен. И давайте без сюрпризов: у нас с вами были семь пятниц на неделе.» (my pa-nee-MA-yem, shto vy see-DEE-tye na mye-LEE, no ee my ne MO-zhem ra-BO-tat see-BYE f oo-BY-tak, ne NA-da DYE-lat eez MOO-khee sla-NA, my ne see-DEEM na mye-LEE, PRO-sta DYEEN-gee pree-DOOT f kants-TSYE MYE-sya-tsa, ha-ra-SHO, da-VAY-tye ne tee-NOOT rye-ZEE-noo, vy PLA-tee-tye pa-la-VEE-noo see-CHAS, pa-la-VEE-noo chye-ryez dvee nee-DYE-lee, sag-LA-sen, ee da-VAY-tye BYEZ syoor-PREE-zaf, oo nas s VA-mee BY-lee syem PYAT-neets na nee-DYE-lye), 'we understand that you are broke, but we cannot work at a loss either. Do not make a mountain out of a molehill. We are not broke, the money simply arrives at the end of the month. Fine, let us not drag it out: you pay half now, half in two weeks. Agreed. And let us have no surprises: you and I have had seven Fridays in a week.' Notice that each idiom is followed by a concrete statement that carries the actual content. The idiom does the facework, the number does the work, and a negotiation without the numbers would be a quarrel. Notice also the repair «не надо делать из мухи слона», which rejects the other side's framing without rejecting the person, the same move lesson 87 described for disagreement.
depth.mistake: Three errors recur. The first is register: putting idioms into a заявление, a report, a contract or a news item, where the genre has no speaker entitled to an opinion. The second is modification: changing the verb's aspect, inserting an adjective, or swapping a synonym, as in тянуть резину becoming тянуть кабель, or не покладая рук becoming не покладая силы, which produces a phrase no Russian recognises. The third is the wrong subject or the wrong direction of evaluation: a project that вылетело в трубу, a plan that бьёт баклуши, денег куры не клюют said about a colleague who is present. Diagnostic for all three: ask who is evaluating whom, and whether the genre allows that evaluation; then check the phrase in a dictionary of idioms rather than in a general dictionary, because a general dictionary will not tell you that the form is frozen.
depth.application: Collect ten idioms of work and money from speech, fiction or a film, and for each one record five things: the literal image, the idiomatic meaning, the evaluation, the kind of subject it takes, and one context where it would be wrong. Then write two texts of six sentences on the same situation, a colleague who missed a deadline, one as a message to a friend and one as a report to a manager, and use at least three idioms in the first and none in the second. Compare the two and list what the idioms added and what they cost. Finally, take the report and rewrite one sentence with an idiom in a way that a Russian reader would accept, which usually means quoting somebody's speech inside the report: «Руководитель отдела отметил, что сотрудник, по его словам, тянул резину». That last move, quoting the idiom as somebody's words rather than using it in your own voice, is how professional writing keeps the colour without taking the stance.
depth.summary: Work and money idioms are fixed units with a frozen grammar and a built-in evaluation, and the evaluation is what limits them. Complimentary idioms such as не покладая рук praise, critical ones such as тянуть резину and бить баклуши judge, self-directed ones such as взять себя в руки and как белка в колесе advise, and the money set moves from mild, сидеть на мели, to loaded, денег куры не клюют. None of them belongs in a document, because a document has no speaker entitled to an opinion. They belong in speech, in messages between colleagues, and inside quotation marks when a report needs to report somebody else's view.
