lessons.title: Weather, health and the proverb: folk expressions and the moment they turn rude
lessons.explanation:
Weather and health are the two domains where Russian speech is most figurative, because both are things people cannot control and therefore comment on. The weather set is small and highly colloquial. «Льёт как из ведра» (lyot kak eez veed-RA), literally 'it is pouring as if out of a bucket', is the standard way to say that it is raining hard; «собачий холод» (sa-BA-cheey KHO-lat), 'dog cold', means bitter cold and is stronger than мороз; «погода шепчет» (pa-GO-da SHEP-chet), 'the weather is whispering', is ironic and means that the weather is inviting you outside, and it only works about pleasant weather, never about a storm. Two of the weather phrases are not about weather at all. «Ждать у моря погоды» (zhdat o MO-rya pa-GO-dy), 'to wait for the weather by the sea', means to wait passively for circumstances to change instead of acting, and it is a criticism. «Делать погоду» (DYE-lat pa-GO-doo), 'to make the weather', means to be the decisive factor, and it takes a person or a factor as its subject: «Решает не цена, а сроки: они делают погоду» (ree-SHA-yet ne tsee-NA, a SRO-kee, a-NEE DYE-la-yut pa-GO-doo), 'it is not the price that decides but the deadlines: they call the tune.'

The health set is equally figurative and even more limited. «Встать не с той ноги» (fstat ne s toy na-GEE), 'to get up on the wrong foot', explains a bad mood and nothing else. «Как рукой сняло» (kak roo-KOY sNYA-la), 'as if removed by a hand', describes pain, fatigue or a bad mood that has vanished, and it is the phrase a Russian uses about a headache that stopped. «Чувствовать себя как огурчик» (CHOOST-va-vat see-BYA kak a-goor-CHEEK), 'to feel like a little cucumber', means fresh and well, and it is mild, slightly humorous, and typically said by or about somebody older; a young man who says it about himself sounds as if he is quoting his grandmother. «Ни жив ни мёртв» (nee zheef nee MYORTF), 'neither alive nor dead', means paralysed by fear, not ill. «Болеть душой за» (ba-LYET doo-SHOY za) plus the accusative, 'to ache with one's soul for', means to worry about somebody, and «прийти в себя» (preet-TEE f see-BYA) means to come round or to recover composure. «На седьмом небе» (na see-DYO-mam NYE-bye), 'on the seventh heaven', is happiness, and «как на иголках» (kak na ee-GOL-kakh), 'as if on needles', is nervous impatience.

None of these belongs in a medical document. «Как рукой сняло» describes a feeling, not a symptom, and a doctor cannot record it; «как огурчик» reports subjective freshness and says nothing about health; «ни жив ни мёртв» describes fear, and using it of a patient's condition would be both wrong and alarming. «Болеть душой за кого-то» is a phrase about the speaker's concern, and saying it to a patient's face can sound intrusive, because it makes the patient responsible for managing the speaker's feelings. The safe rule is the one lesson 125 gave for register: these phrases report an evaluation, and a medical record does not carry evaluations.

A пословица (pa-SLO-vee-tsa), 'proverb', is one step further out, because it is a complete sentence with a generic subject rather than a phrase with a meaning. «Век живи, век учись» (VYEK zhee-VEE, VYEK oo-CHEES), 'live a century, learn a century', comments on a lesson learned late. «Семь раз отмерь, один раз отрежь» (SYEM raz at-MYER, a-DEEN raz at-RYECH), 'measure seven times, cut once', advises caution before an irreversible act. «Тише едешь, дальше будешь» (TEE-sheh YE-dyesh, DAL-sheh BOO-desh), 'the quieter you drive, the further you will get', advises patience. «Не имей сто рублей, а имей сто друзей» (ne ee-MYEY STO roo-BLYEY, a ee-MYEY STO droo-ZYEY), 'do not have a hundred roubles, have a hundred friends', values people over money. «Работа не волк, в лес не убежит» (ra-BO-ta ne volk, v lyes ne oo-bee-ZHEET), 'work is not a wolf, it will not run off into the forest', is a joke about postponing work. «Не всё то золото, что блестит» (ne vsyo to ZO-la-ta, shto blyes-TEET), 'not everything that glitters is gold', warns against appearances.

The difference between a proverb and a поговорка (pa-ga-VOR-ka), 'saying', is grammatical: a proverb is a whole sentence that can stand alone, while a saying is a fragment that needs a sentence around it, as денег куры не клюют did in lesson 128. That difference matters because a proverb brings its own subject and its own mood, and those are what collide with a document. A proverb argues by tradition rather than by evidence, and tradition speaks with the authority of an elder; that is why a proverb between equals is wisdom and a proverb from a subordinate to a superior is a lecture. The frame «как говорится» (kak ga-va-REE-tsya), 'as they say', is the standard way to quote a proverb and hand the authority back to the tradition, which is why it softens the moralising even when the proverb itself does not change.
lessons.example:
A spoken exchange where the proverbs work. «Ты слышал, что проект опять перенесли?» «Слышал. Ну и что, работа не волк, в лес не убежит.» «Это ты начальнику скажи.» «Я и говорю: семь раз отмерь, один раз отрежь. Может, перенос к лучшему.» «Как говорится, не было бы счастья, да несчастье помогло.» (ty SLY-shal, shto pra-YEKT a-PYAT pee-ree-nee-SLEE, SLY-shal, noo ee shto, ra-BO-ta ne volk, v lyes ne oo-bee-ZHEET, EH-ta ty na-CHAL-nee-koo ska-ZHEE, ya ee ga-va-RYOO, SYEM raz at-MYER, a-DEEN raz at-RYECH, MO-zhet, pee-ree-NOS k LOOT-she-moo, kak ga-va-REE-tsya, NE BY-la by SHCHAS-tya, da nee-SHCHAS-tye pa-mag-LO), 'did you hear the project has been postponed again? I did. So what, work is not a wolf, it will not run into the forest. Tell that to the boss. That is what I am saying: measure seven times, cut once. Maybe the postponement is for the best. As they say, every cloud has a silver lining.' Four proverbs in five turns, and the exchange works because the speakers are equals, the mood is ironic, and every proverb is followed by a concrete statement that carries the actual opinion.

Now the same proverb in a letter about a two-month delay: «Уважаемый Андрей Петрович! Напоминаю, что поставка по договору № 14 задержана на два месяца. Как говорится, тише едешь, дальше будешь. Прошу сообщить новые сроки.» (na-pee-mee-NA-yoo, shto pas-TAF-ka pa da-ga-VO-roo chye-TYR-na-tsat za-DYER-zha-na na dva MYE-sya-tsa, kak ga-va-REE-tsya, TEE-sheh YE-dyesh, DAL-sheh BOO-desh, pra-SHOO sa-ap-SHCHEET NO-vy-ye SRO-kee), 'dear Andrei Petrovich, I remind you that the delivery under contract 14 is two months late. As they say, the quieter you drive the further you will get. Please inform me of the new deadlines.' The proverb says that patience is rewarded, which in this position reads either as consent to the delay or as sarcasm, and the letter ends by asking for dates, so the reader cannot tell whether the writer is angry or amused. Two repairs are available. Either remove the proverb and let the dates do the work: «Поставка задержана на два месяца. Прошу сообщить новые сроки в течение трёх дней.» Or keep the irony but mark it as a quotation from somebody else, which is the technique lesson 128 ended with: «Руководитель отдела заметил, что, как говорится, тише едешь, дальше будешь, но договор устанавливает иной срок.» That version is still risky, and a professional writer would simply drop it.

A third context shows where a proverb is not merely weak but insulting. In a negotiation, after the other side has presented an offer: «Не всё то золото, что блестит» (ne vsyo to ZO-la-ta, shto blyes-TEET), 'not everything that glitters is gold.' The proverb is about the offer, but its generic second person addresses the person who made it, and the implication is that they are trying to deceive you. Between colleagues who know each other the same words are a joke; across a table between strangers they are an accusation. The proverb has not changed; the relationship has.
lessons.question: In a letter to a supplier about a two-month delay you write «Как говорится, тише едешь, дальше будешь». Why is this a mistake, and what does the letter need instead?
lessons.answer: The proverb advises patience, so in a letter about a breach it reads as consent to the delay or as mockery; the letter needs the dates, the contract reference and a demand with a period, not folk wisdom.
lessons.distractor: There is no mistake; proverbs make Russian letters warmer, and a Russian supplier will appreciate the friendly tone.
lessons.correction: The proverb fails for three reasons that compound. Its content contradicts the complaint: тише едешь recommends going slowly, and the letter is complaining about slowness, so the sentence either withdraws the complaint or mocks the supplier. Its grammar contradicts the genre: a proverb is a complete sentence with a generic subject, so it speaks in the voice of tradition, and in a business letter that voice belongs to nobody the writer is entitled to borrow. And its position contradicts the request: the letter ends by asking for new deadlines, and a reader who has just been told that slow is good cannot tell whether the deadlines are a demand or a joke. The repair is not another proverb but the four-sentence claim skeleton of lesson 122: the facts, «поставка задержана на два месяца», the basis, «в соответствии с пунктом 5 договора», the demand, «прошу сообщить новые сроки в течение трёх дней», and the consequence. Irony can be kept, but only if it is attributed to somebody else and the demand still stands on its own.

depth.definitions: A пословица is a fixed complete sentence with a generalised subject that states a piece of folk wisdom; a поговорка is a fixed phrase that names a situation without forming a sentence, as денег куры не клюют does. A фразеологизм is the general term for a fixed multi-word unit and covers both. Обобщённое лицо (a-bab-SHCHON-na-ye lee-TSO), 'generalised person', is the grammatical property that makes a proverb sound like a rule for everybody rather than a statement about one situation, and it is what turns a proverb into a lecture when it is addressed to a particular person. The frame как говорится marks a quotation from tradition and shifts the authority away from the speaker. Экспрессивная лексика is vocabulary carrying evaluation, and the weather and health idioms are all expressive. Prerequisites: the idioms and their register limits in lesson 128, the stance particles of lesson 102, the register ladder of lesson 125, the complaint letter of lesson 122, and the irony of lesson 93.
depth.mechanism: A proverb persuades by invoking a shared tradition, and that is both its power and its limit. The argument is not evidence but authority: the sentence is old, everybody knows it, and therefore it settles the matter. Authority of that kind works between people who accept the same tradition as binding, which is why proverbs flourish among peers, in families, in toasts and in advice, and fail in institutions, where the binding authority is a document. The grammatical mechanism reinforces the social one. The generic second person of тише едешь addresses anybody, so when it is used on a particular person it silently repositions the speaker as an elder entitled to instruct. The frame как говорится is the escape hatch: by marking the sentence as a quotation, the speaker transfers the authority to the tradition and keeps only the role of a reporter, which is why the same proverb can be acceptable with the frame and rude without it. The health idioms work by a different mechanism, metonymy, where a bodily image stands for a state: как рукой сняло for sudden relief, как огурчик for freshness. Metonymy is why they cannot be used in a medical record, because the image reports a feeling rather than a finding.
depth.secondExample: A meeting where the same proverb fails, and the repair. A junior analyst, asked why the figures are late: «Как говорится, семь раз отмерь, один раз отрежь: я перепроверял данные.» (kak ga-va-REE-tsya, SYEM raz at-MYER, a-DEEN raz at-RYECH, ya pee-ree-pra-vye-RYAL DAN-ny-ye), 'as they say, measure seven times, cut once: I was rechecking the data.' The proverb is meant as a justification, and it lands as a reproach to the room, because it implies that everybody else is cutting before measuring. The manager's answer is likely to be about the deadline, not about the proverb, which means the analyst has lost the argument by winning the aphorism. The repair is to drop the proverb and state the trade-off in numbers: «Я перепроверял данные: это заняло два дня. Если нужно быстрее, могу сдать сегодня с точностью до десятых.» That sentence keeps the same justification and adds a choice, which is what a meeting can act on. Notice that the proverb was not wrong about the world; it was wrong about the genre, because a meeting allocates work and does not award wisdom.
depth.mistake: Three errors recur, all of them about the relationship rather than the words. The first is putting a proverb into a document, where the genre has no speaker entitled to folk authority; the symptom is a letter that sounds either whimsical or passive-aggressive. The second is addressing a proverb to a superior or a client, where the generic second person turns into a lecture; the symptom is a silence after the sentence. The third is using a proverb whose image contradicts the situation, as тише едешь does in a complaint about delay and как огурчик does in a report about illness. There is also a comprehension error worth naming: работа не волк, в лес не убежит does not mean that work is dangerous or that one should work hard, it means that work can wait, and learners who use it as encouragement produce the opposite of what they intend. Diagnostic for all four: ask who is entitled to give advice in this situation, and whether the proverb's image supports the point or undermines it.
depth.application: Collect eight proverbs and for each one write two things: the speech act it performs (advice, consolation, warning, reproach, joke) and one context where it works and one where it fails. Then write a short dialogue between two colleagues in which three proverbs are used correctly, and the same content as a letter to a client, with every proverb replaced by a fact, a date or a number. Read both aloud and notice which one takes longer to say and which one takes longer to act on. Finally, take one health idiom and one weather idiom and write a sentence in which each is used well, then a sentence in which each is used badly, and label what went wrong in the second. The pair of sentences for each idiom is the useful output, because it fixes the boundary rather than the phrase.
depth.summary: Weather and health idioms are figurative, evaluative and strictly conversational: льёт как из ведра, собачий холод, как рукой сняло, как огурчик, ни жив ни мёртв all report a feeling or a judgement and none of them belongs in a medical record. A proverb goes further, because it is a complete sentence with a generalised subject, and its authority is tradition rather than evidence. That authority works between equals and fails in documents, towards superiors, and whenever the proverb's image contradicts the point being made. The frame как говорится marks the quotation and softens it, but it cannot save a proverb that argues against your own letter.

visual.title: Proverb gate: five questions before the sentence leaves your mouth
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: a vertical gate with five yes or no questions, an arrow labelled use it leading to a speech context, an arrow labelled drop it leading to a rewritten sentence, and a margin list of the four failure modes.
steps: Step 1, draw the gate with five questions stacked vertically. Question one: am I speaking or writing? Question two: is the addressee my equal, my superior or a client? Question three: does the proverb's advice point the same way as my argument? Question four: is the proverb's subject the same kind of thing as my subject? Question five: have I marked it with как говорится or attributed it to somebody?

Step 2, draw the no exit. Any answer that puts the sentence in writing, towards a superior, against the argument or on the wrong subject sends it down the arrow labelled drop it, and the arrow ends in a box labelled rewrite with a fact, a date or a number.

Step 3, draw the yes exit. Five answers that keep it in speech, among equals, pointing the same way, on the right subject and marked as a quotation send it down the arrow labelled use it, and the arrow ends in a box labelled follow with a concrete statement, because a proverb never carries the content on its own.

Step 4, fill the margin with the four failure modes: document, superior, contradictory image, wrong subject. Beside each write the example from this lesson, тише едешь in the delay letter, семь раз отмерь in the meeting, работа не волк used as encouragement, and не всё то золото across a negotiation table.

Step 5, add the repair column. For each failure mode write the replacement: a fact, a date, a number, and an attributed quotation. The replacements are the same four moves as the claim skeleton of lesson 122, which is why the two lessons belong to the same unit.

Step 6, run one proverb through the gate. Take a proverb you like, answer the five questions for a real message you have to send, and write both outcomes, the sentence you would have sent and the sentence the gate produced.

lessons.title: False friends: the words an English or Spanish speaker will actually get wrong
lessons.explanation:
Ложные друзья переводчика (LOZH-ny-ye droo-ZYA pee-ree-VOT-chee-ka), 'the translator's false friends', are words that look like a word in your language and mean something else. They are dangerous for a reason that has nothing to do with difficulty: the form is familiar, so the learner stops checking, and the sentence that results is grammatical, comprehensible and wrong. The classic English cases are lexical. Актуальный (ak-too-AL-ny) means 'topical, important now', not 'actual', which is фактический or действительный: «актуальный вопрос» (ak-too-AL-ny vap-ROS) is a question that matters at the moment, while «фактический вопрос» is a question about the facts. Симпатичный (seem-pa-TEECH-ny) means 'attractive, likeable', not 'sympathetic', which is сочувствующий (sa-CHOOST-voo-yoo-shcheey). Рецепт (ree-TSEPT) means both 'recipe' and 'prescription' and never 'receipt', which is чек (chek) or квитанция (kvee-TAN-tsee-ya). Фамилия (fa-MEE-lee-ya) is 'surname', not 'family', which is семья (see-MYA). Кабинет (ka-bee-NET) is an office, a study or a consulting room, not a piece of furniture, which is шкаф (shkaf). Магазин (ma-ga-ZEEN) is a shop, not a magazine, which is журнал (zhoor-NAL). Декада (dee-KA-da) is a ten-day period, not a decade, which is десятилетие (dee-see-tee-LYE-tee-ye). Балл (bal) is a grade or a score, not a ball, which is мяч (myach). Аудитория (a-oo-dee-TO-ree-ya) is a lecture hall or the people in it, not 'auditory'. Принципиальный (preen-tsee-pee-AL-ny) is 'principled', not 'principal', which is главный (GLAV-ny).

The Spanish-speaking learner has a different profile, and it is worth stating precisely because it changes what to practise. Some Spanish words transfer correctly: simpático and receta line up with симпатичный and рецепт in the relevant senses, so a Spanish speaker is less likely to err there than an English speaker. Others do not. Spanish actual means 'current, present-day', which is closer to актуальный than English actual is but still not identical, because актуальный adds the idea of relevance and urgency: «актуальная информация» is information that is up to date and matters, while текущий is merely current. Spanish gabinete is a cabinet in the political sense or a study, and its Russian counterpart кабинет follows the room rather than the government. Spanish pretensión overlaps with претензия (pree-TEN-zee-ya), which means a claim or a complaint and, in the plural, pretensions, so the two languages are close but the Russian word belongs to the legal register that lesson 122 used. And Spanish década, like English decade, is ten years, while декада is ten days, a word that Russian institutions use for a ten-day campaign or festival and that a learner will meet in university and cultural contexts.

There is a second family of false friends that no dictionary of interlingual pairs will list, because both words are Russian: паронимы (pa-RO-nee-my), 'paronyms', pairs built from one root with different prefixes or suffixes, both correct, both frequent, and easy to confuse in exactly the registers this pack covers. Предоставить (pree-das-TA-veet) means 'to grant, to provide' and pairs with отпуск, документы, слово, отсрочку, кредит. Представить (preet-STA-veet) means 'to present, to introduce, to imagine' and pairs with отчёт, проект, гостя, себе. The two are one prefix apart, and the wrong one turns a заявление into nonsense: «Прошу представить мне отпуск» says 'I ask that leave be presented to me', which is not a thing. Эффективный (ef-fek-TEEV-ny) is 'effective' and эффектный (ef-FYEKT-ny) is 'striking, showy'; a presentation can be эффектная and a manager эффективный, and mixing them compliments the wrong quality. Экономический (e-ka-na-MEE-ches-keey) is 'economic', about the economy, while экономичный (e-ka-na-MEECH-ny) is 'economical', about saving money. Одень (a-DYEN) takes a person and надень (na-DYEN) takes a garment: одеть ребёнка, надеть пальто. Оплатить (ap-la-TEET) takes the thing paid, оплатить счёт, while заплатить (za-pla-TEET) takes за plus the thing: заплатить за обед.

What unites the two families is that context rarely rescues you. «Актуальный вопрос» and «фактический вопрос» are both plausible phrases, «представить отпуск» and «предоставить отпуск» both parse, and a reader who is not looking for the error will supply the intended meaning and move on. That is why false friends survive years of study: the feedback that would correct them never arrives.
lessons.example:
A workplace email with four false friends, three of them wrong. «Уважаемая Анна Сергеевна! Направляю вам актуальный отчёт за апрель. В кабинете 312 мы обсудили рецепт договора. Прошу представить мне отпуск с 1 июня. Мой фамилия указана в приложении.» (oo-va-ZHA-ye-ma-YA A-na syer-GYE-yev-na, nap-rav-LYA-yoo vam ak-too-AL-ny at-CHOT za ap-RYEL, f ka-bee-NYE-tye TREE-sta dvee-NA-tsat my ab-soo-DEE-lee ree-TSEPT da-ga-VO-ra, pra-SHOO preet-STA-veet mnye OT-poosk s PIR-va-va EY-oo-nya, moy fa-MEE-lee-ya oo-KA-za-na f pree-la-ZHYE-nee-ee), 'dear Anna Sergeevna, I am sending you the current report for April. In room 312 we discussed the recipe of the contract. I ask that leave be presented to me from 1 June. My surname is indicated in the enclosure.' Four errors and one correct item. Актуальный is used correctly here, as 'current and relevant', which is the sense that survives. Рецепт договора is wrong twice: a contract has no recipe, and the word the writer wants is, depending on the meaning, условия договора, 'the terms of the contract', or проект договора, 'the draft contract', which is the paronym of рецепт in sound if not in root. Представить отпуск should be предоставить. And мой фамилия is wrong in gender, because фамилия is feminine: моя фамилия, a reminder that a false friend also brings its own grammar.

The corrected version: «Уважаемая Анна Сергеевна! Направляю вам актуальный отчёт за апрель. В кабинете 312 мы обсудили условия договора. Прошу предоставить мне отпуск с 1 июня. Моя фамилия указана в приложении.» The paragraph has not changed its content at all, which is the point: false friends are never about what you meant, only about which word carries it.

A second context, a clinic, where the same word appears in its other sense: «Рецепт на лекарство можно получить у врача в кабинете 12. Возьмите рецепт и чек из аптеки.» (ree-TSEPT na lee-KAR-stva MOZH-na pa-loo-CHEET oo vra-CHA f ka-bee-NYE-tye dvee-NA-tsat, vaz-MEE-tye ree-TSEPT ee chek eez ap-TYE-kee), 'a prescription for the medicine can be obtained from the doctor in room 12. Take the prescription and the receipt from the pharmacy.' Here рецепт is the prescription, чек is the receipt, and кабинет is the consulting room, three words that an English speaker would distribute differently: 'recipe', 'receipt' and 'cabinet' would all be wrong, and each wrong word would be understood in a way that matters.
lessons.question: Your заявление reads «Прошу представить мне отпуск». A clerk corrects it to «предоставить». Why does one prefix make the difference between a document and nonsense?
lessons.answer: Предоставить means to grant or provide and is the verb that collocates with отпуск, документы, слово and отсрочка; представить means to present, introduce or imagine, so представить отпуск has no referent.
lessons.distractor: The two verbs are interchangeable in official style, and the clerk is enforcing a personal preference rather than a rule.
lessons.correction: The pair split historically and the split is now lexical, not stylistic. Предоставить is built with the prefix предо- and carries the sense of placing something at somebody's disposal: предоставить отпуск, предоставить документы, предоставить слово, предоставить отсрочку, предоставить кредит. Представить is built with пре- and carries the sense of putting something before somebody, physically or mentally: представить отчёт, представить проект, представить гостя, представить себе, 'to imagine'. The collocations are the test, and they do not overlap. A learner who writes представить отпуск has not made a stylistic choice; they have used a verb whose object list does not include отпуск, which is why the clerk's correction is a correction and not a preference. The same trap produces представить документы, which is wrong for the same reason, and представить к награде, which is right because that is a different collocation meaning 'to nominate for an award'. The general lesson: when two Russian words differ by a prefix and both exist, the dictionary entry for each will list its objects, and those lists are the rule.

depth.definitions: Ложные друзья переводчика are words in two languages that resemble each other and differ in meaning; межъязыковая омонимия (myezh-yee-zee-ka-VA-ya a-ma-nee-MEE-ya), 'interlingual homonymy', is the technical name. Паронимы are words in one language built from the same root with different affixes, both existing and both frequent, such as предоставить and представить or эффективный and эффектный. A калька (KAL-ka) is a loan translation, a phrase built word by word from another language, and many false-friend errors are calques: сделать решение is a calque of make a decision, and it survives because each word is Russian. Ложная аналогия is the reasoning error behind the whole family, the assumption that a familiar form predicts a familiar meaning. Prerequisites: the prefix system of lesson 106, which is what produces the paronym pairs, the nominalisation and register material of lesson 125, the document collocations of lesson 121, and the claim vocabulary of lesson 122, where претензия first appeared in its legal sense.
depth.mechanism: False friends work by exploiting a shortcut that normal reading depends on. A fluent reader recognises words by shape and predicts meaning from frequency, and that prediction is usually right, which is why it is trusted; a false friend is a case where the prediction is wrong and nothing in the sentence flags it. The interlingual cases are accidents of shared etymology or of loanwords that took different paths: магазин came from French magasin, 'warehouse, shop', while English magazine took the sense of a storehouse of articles, and both are legitimate developments of the same source. The intralingual cases are accidents of the prefix system: предоставить and представить both descend from ставить, 'to place', and the prefixes пре- and предо- once distinguished a mental placing from a real one, but the modern verbs have drifted into separate collocational sets. In both families the error is invisible because the wrong word is real, common and syntactically well behaved. The only reliable defence is a monolingual dictionary consulted for the word's own collocations, because a bilingual dictionary organised by English meaning will send you to the wrong Russian word, and a spellchecker will not object to a word that exists.
depth.secondExample: A curriculum vitae and a form, where the false friends are institutional. «Фамилия: Соколова. Имя: Мария. Отчество: Сергеевна. Дата рождения: 12 мая 2004 года. Образование: студентка второго курса исторического факультета. Балл за экзамен: 85. Адрес электронной почты: указан в анкете.» (fa-MEE-lee-ya sa-ka-LO-va, EE-mya ma-REE-ya, OT-ches-tva syer-GYE-yev-na, DA-ta razh-DYE-nee-ya dvee-NA-tsa-ta-va MA-ya dvee TY-see-chee chye-TYR-na-tsa-ta-va GO-da, ab-ra-za-VA-nee-ye stoo-DYENT-ka fta-RO-va KOR-sa ees-ta-REE-ches-ka-va fa-kool-TYE-ta, BAL za ek-ZA-men VO-sem-dee-syat pyat, A-drees e-lek-TRON-nay POCH-ty oo-KA-zan f an-KYE-tye), 'surname: Sokolova. First name: Maria. Patronymic: Sergeevna. Date of birth: 12 May 2004. Education: second-year student of the history faculty. Examination score: 85. Email address: given in the form.' Every label here is a trap for somebody: фамилия is not family, балл is not ball, анкета is not a questionnaire in the English sense but the form itself, and отчество has no English equivalent at all, which is why the label is usually left untranslated in Russian documents issued abroad. Note too that the labels are in the nominative and followed by a colon, which is the form convention: «Фамилия: Соколова», not «Фамилия Соколова», and the value stays in the nominative because it is a label and not a sentence.
depth.mistake: Five errors recur. The first is the interlingual substitution, актуальный for 'actual', рецепт for 'receipt', магазин for 'magazine', each produced by trusting the shape. The second is the paronym, представить for предоставить, эффектный for эффективный, экономический for экономичный, where both words exist and only the collocation decides. The third is a calque phrase built from correct words, сделать решение, принимать меры in the sense of 'take measures' is right but брать меры is not, and играть значение. The fourth is a gender or agreement error triggered by the false friend, as in мой фамилия, because the Russian noun's gender is not the gender of the English word the learner had in mind. The fifth is overcorrection: having learned that актуальный is not 'actual', a learner avoids the word entirely and writes фактический in a sentence where актуальный was correct. Diagnostic for all five: look the Russian word up in a monolingual dictionary and read its collocations, not its translation; if the dictionary does not list your object after your verb, the pair is wrong, whatever the bilingual dictionary said.
depth.application: Start a personal false-friend list from your own writing rather than from a textbook. Go through ten emails or documents you have written in Russian and underline every word you chose by translating from English or Spanish. Look each one up in a monolingual dictionary, for instance the Russian Wiktionary, and record four things: the word, the meaning you assumed, the meaning the dictionary gives, and one collocation that proves the difference. Then write five sentences in which the false friend is used correctly and five in which the word you would have used is replaced by the right one, and have a Russian speaker mark which of the ten sound native. Finally, add the paronym pairs to the same list, предоставить against представить, эффективный against эффектный, оплатить against заплатить, and write one document sentence for each member of each pair. The list, not the lesson, is what will keep the errors out of your next заявление.
depth.summary: False friends are words that look familiar and mean something else, and they survive because the sentence remains comprehensible. The interlingual set is lexical: актуальный is topical, симпатичный is attractive, рецепт is recipe or prescription, фамилия is surname, кабинет is a room, магазин is a shop, декада is ten days, балл is a score. The intralingual set is paronyms: предоставить against представить, эффективный against эффектный, экономический against экономичный, оплатить against заплатить. Both families are invisible to context and to spellcheckers, so the only defence is a monolingual dictionary read for collocations. In documents the stakes are highest, because the wrong word is not misunderstood, it is filed.

readings.title: Википедия, «Ложные друзья переводчика»
readings.note: Read the lead and the sections on the causes of the phenomenon and on the main types, which distinguish complete false friends from partial ones whose meanings overlap in some senses. The partial category is the one that matters for актуальный and претензия, because a partial false friend is right often enough to keep the learner confident. Caveat: the article is long, its examples are drawn from many language pairs, and the Russian-English section is only one part of it, so read the typology and check particular pairs elsewhere.

readings.title: Wikipedia, 'False friend'
readings.note: Read the lead and the section on causes, which names loanwords, shared etymology and coincidence as the three sources. The etymological section explains why магазин and magazine diverge from a common French source, which is the clearest single illustration of how a false friend arises without anybody making a mistake. Caveat: the article is comparative and English-centred, and it contains a great many examples from language pairs that are not relevant here, so read the causes rather than the lists.

readings.title: Викисловарь, «актуальный»
readings.note: Read the Значение section and the stress, актуа́льный. The definition gives the sense of being important or relevant at the present moment, which is the sense this lesson insists on, and the declension table is a reminder that the adjective agrees with its noun in a way the English word does not. Caveat: the entry is a dictionary, so it records the meaning but not the frequency or the register, and it will not tell you that актуальный is common in journalism and in business speech.

readings.title: Викисловарь, «рецепт»
readings.note: Read the Значение section, where the culinary and medical senses are listed separately, and note that neither of them is 'receipt'. The entry is the best short proof that a single Russian word can cover two English words while missing a third, which is the structural reason false friends are unpredictable. Caveat: the entry does not discuss the confusion with чек, so add that pair yourself and check чек in the same dictionary.

visual.title: False-friend triage card: shape, assumed meaning, real meaning, collocations, replacement
visual.description: A labelled text diagram: a card with five fields across the top and a stack of rows, one per word; a red margin column lists the correct Russian word for the assumed meaning, and a bottom strip holds the paronym pairs.
steps: Step 1, draw the card with five fields: the Russian word, the word it resembles, the meaning you assumed, the meaning the dictionary gives, and one collocation that proves it. Fill the first row for актуальный: resembles actual, assumed 'actual', dictionary 'topical, relevant now', collocation актуальный вопрос.

Step 2, fill the replacement column. For each row write the Russian word that does mean the assumed thing: фактический for actual, сочувствующий for sympathetic, чек for receipt, семья for family, шкаф for cabinet, журнал for magazine, десятилетие for decade, мяч for ball. The column is the practical output of the card.

Step 3, add the partial-overlap rows in a different colour. Актуальный and претензия belong here, because their meanings overlap with the English or Spanish word in some senses and not others; write the overlapping sense and the non-overlapping sense side by side, since partial friends are the ones that keep you confident.

Step 4, add the bottom strip for paronyms, four pairs on one line each: предоставить against представить, эффективный against эффектный, экономический against экономичный, оплатить against заплатить. Under each pair write the object list that separates them: отпуск, документы, слово against отчёт, проект, себе; задача, метод against дизайн, жест; рост, crisis against автомобиль; счёт against за обед.

Step 5, add the checking rule at the foot of the card. One line: look the Russian word up in a monolingual dictionary and read its collocations, not its translation. Write beside it the reason: a bilingual dictionary is organised by the meaning you started from, which is the meaning that misled you.

Step 6, run three of your own sentences through the card. For each sentence, find the word you chose by translation, fill a row, and rewrite the sentence with the word from the replacement column. If the rewrite changes nothing, the original was right and you have learned a pair that does not apply to you.

russianItems.meaning: to present, to introduce, to imagine (perfective)

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so that it reads as idiomatic Russian: «На совещании мы ___ решение продлить договор».
questions.answer: приняли
questions.distractor: сделали
questions.correction: The noun решение selects the verb принять, and the aspect is perfective because the decision was taken once at one meeting. Сделали решение is a calque of make a decision: it is comprehensible, which is why it survives, but no Russian writes it. The same noun appears in вынести решение, which is what a court does, and in принимать решение, which is the repeated or ongoing version.

questions.prompt: Choose the form: «Согласно ___ оплата производится в течение десяти банковских дней».
questions.answer: договору
questions.distractor: договора
questions.correction: Согласно belongs to the closed set of four dative words, according to, thanks to, contrary to and in defiance of, so the noun takes the dative. The genitive feels right because it is the default for derived prepositions and because the compound phrases in -ние, в течение, в целях, на основании, all take it, and a learner who reads contracts has seen a hundred genitives.

questions.prompt: A colleague asks how you are managing financially this month. Which idiom means that you are short of money?
questions.answer: «Сижу на мели.»
questions.distractor: «Бью баклуши.»
questions.correction: Сидеть на мели means to be broke, literally to sit on a shoal, and it is the mildest of the money idioms. Бить баклуши means to idle and has nothing to do with money; a learner who confuses the two tells a colleague that they are lazy when they mean that they are poor. Both are colloquial, and neither belongs in a report or an application.

questions.prompt: You are writing to a supplier about a two-month delay. Which version of the closing paragraph belongs in the letter?
questions.answer: «Поставка задержана на два месяца. Прошу сообщить новые сроки в течение трёх дней.»
questions.distractor: «Как говорится, тише едешь, дальше будешь.»
questions.correction: The proverb advises patience, so in a complaint about slowness it withdraws the complaint or mocks the supplier, and its generic second person addresses the reader as if the writer were entitled to give advice. The first version gives the fact and the demand with a period, which is what a letter can act on. A proverb can survive in a letter only if it is attributed to somebody else and the demand still stands on its own.

questions.prompt: A clerk corrects your заявление from «Прошу представить мне отпуск» to «Прошу предоставить мне отпуск». What separates the two verbs?
questions.answer: Предоставить means to grant or provide and collocates with отпуск, документы, слово and отсрочка; представить means to present, introduce or imagine and collocates with отчёт, проект, гостя and себе.
questions.distractor: Nothing separates them; the two verbs are interchangeable in official style and the clerk is enforcing a preference.
questions.correction: The pair is a paronym, one prefix apart, and the difference is lexical rather than stylistic: each verb has its own list of objects, and отпуск is not on the list of представить. The same trap produces представить документы, which is wrong, and представить к награде, which is right because that collocation means to nominate for an award. The test is always the object list in a monolingual dictionary.

questions.prompt: Which element of a заявление is the only one that speaks in the first person?
questions.answer: The request section introduced by прошу.
questions.distractor: The applicant block in the header, which begins with от.
questions.correction: The header is a genitive noun phrase with no verb and no subject, so it cannot speak in the first person; adding я there turns the document into an explanation. The body is a performative, and прошу is the first person that creates the request. The addressee sits in the dative, the applicant in the genitive, and only the request section says я, usually without the pronoun.

questions.prompt: Which sentence states a period that the other side can be held to?
questions.answer: «Прошу в течение десяти дней с момента получения претензии вернуть уплаченную сумму.»
questions.distractor: «Прошу немедленно вернуть уплаченную сумму.»
questions.correction: Немедленно cannot be measured, so it gives the recipient nothing to comply with and a court nothing to enforce. A claim measures the period either from a stated event, с момента получения, or from the contract, в течение срока, предусмотренного пунктом 5.2. The number itself often comes from the statute, which is why the letter echoes the legal wording instead of inventing a deadline.

questions.prompt: You need to write to a professor you have never met. Which address form is correct?
questions.answer: «Уважаемый Пётр Андреевич!»
questions.distractor: «Уважаемый Пётр!»
questions.correction: Russian formal address uses the first name with the patronymic and no surname, so the addressee is named as an adult official person. A bare first name after уважаемый mixes the most formal adjective with the most intimate noun form, and the reader cannot tell whether the writer is proposing ты or вы. «Дорогой Пётр Андреевич» would claim a friendship that does not exist.

questions.prompt: The line breaks up during a call. Which sentence blames the connection rather than the person?
questions.answer: «Вас не слышно, связь прерывается. Перезвоните, пожалуйста.»
questions.distractor: «Вы говорите слишком тихо, говорите громче.»
questions.correction: The repair phrases describe the line, which is nobody's fault, and then ask for an action with пожалуйста. The second version attributes the problem to the other person's voice, which in a Russian office reads as a complaint about them rather than about the technology, and the imperfective imperative говорите sounds like a repeated instruction. Перезвоните is perfective because the callback is one event.

questions.prompt: Which request is both polite and specific enough to be acted on?
questions.answer: «Не могли бы вы направить счёт повторно до пятницы?»
questions.distractor: «Не могли бы Вы, если Вас не затруднит, возможно, рассмотреть нашу просьбу о счёте?»
questions.correction: One hedge plus a specific action and a deadline is a request; three hedges plus a vague object is a sentence that asks for a review of a request. Возможно turns the sentence into a question about whether anything is possible, and the reader cannot tell what is wanted. The polite frame does not need reinforcement, it needs an object and a date.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct aspect: «Мы ___ такие решения каждый квартал».
questions.answer: принимаем
questions.distractor: примем
questions.correction: The adverb каждый квартал marks a repeated action, so the imperfective принимаем is required; the perfective примем would report one future decision. The noun решение does not change with aspect, which is why the pair has to be memorised with both verbs. The mistake is common because learners memorise the perfective form first, as the dictionary entry lists it.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is written correctly?
questions.answer: «В течение месяца мы провели проверку и устранили недостатки.»
questions.distractor: «В течении месяца мы провели проверку и устранили недостатки.»
questions.correction: В течение is a preposition meaning within and ends in -ее; в течении with -ии is the prepositional case of the noun течение, current, as in в течении реки. The two are heard identically, which is why the spelling has to be learned as a pair. The same test separates вследствие from в следствие and по истечении from a mistaken по истечение.

questions.prompt: A report needs to say that the department worked at full capacity. Which wording belongs in the report?
questions.answer: «Отдел работал с полной нагрузкой.»
questions.distractor: «Отдел работал не покладая рук.»
questions.correction: Не покладая рук is a complimentary idiom that puts the writer's evaluation into the sentence, and a report has no speaker entitled to praise. The neutral phrase states the fact without the stance. The idiom can still appear in a report if it is quoted as somebody's words, but then it is reported speech rather than the report's own voice.

questions.prompt: In which situation does a proverb do its proper work?
questions.answer: Two colleagues, after a missed deadline, one says «Работа не волк, в лес не убежит», and they both laugh.
questions.distractor: A junior employee writes the same proverb in a letter to a client explaining why the delivery is late.
questions.correction: A proverb argues by tradition and speaks with a generalised voice, so it works between equals who share the evaluation and fails when it is addressed downward or written into a document. In the letter the proverb contradicts the complaint and positions the writer as an elder entitled to advise the client. The frame как говорится marks it as a quotation, but it cannot make a proverb agree with the argument it is undermining.

questions.prompt: A pharmacy receipt is «чек», a doctor's prescription is «рецепт». Which sentence uses the pair correctly?
questions.answer: «Возьмите рецепт у врача и сохраните чек из аптеки.»
questions.distractor: «Возьмите чек у врача и сохраните рецепт из аптеки.»
questions.correction: Рецепт is the prescription the doctor writes and also a recipe; чек is the till receipt. The reversed version swaps the two because English receipt and Russian рецепт look alike, and the sentence remains comprehensible, which is why the error survives. Квитанция is the other word for a receipt, used for payments and official documents rather than for a shop till.

questions.prompt: You need to ask a dean for a deferral in writing. Which sentence combines the document frame with the right collocation?
questions.answer: «Прошу предоставить мне отсрочку до 20 июня в связи с болезнью.»
questions.distractor: «Прошу представить мне отсрочку до 20 июня по причине болезнь.»
questions.correction: The document frame is прошу plus the infinitive, the collocation is предоставить отсрочку, and the ground is в связи с plus the instrumental. The second version uses the paronym представить, which does not take отсрочка, and it produces the wrong case after по причине, which requires the genitive болезни. Both errors are typical of writing assembled from a bilingual dictionary rather than from a model document.

questions.prompt: Which rewrite unpacks the nominalisations of «Осуществление проверки исполнения обязательств необходимо в целях предотвращения нарушений»?
questions.answer: «Нужно проверить, как исполняются обязательства, чтобы не допустить нарушений.»
questions.distractor: «Необходима проверка исполнения обязательств в целях предотвращения нарушений.»
questions.correction: Unpacking restores a verb and an actor for each verbal noun: осуществление проверки becomes проверить, исполнение обязательств becomes как исполняются обязательства, and в целях предотвращения becomes чтобы не допустить. The second version only replaces одно adjective-like word with another and leaves the genitive chain intact. The test is whether a listener can name who does what, and only the first version answers that question.
